title: Loom settings file
description: Server settings, one per LOOM_<NAME> environment variable, named in lowercase. The environment and the dotenv file win over this file; secrets are refused here. Generated by python scripts/codegen/settings_schema.py.

acl_watermark_max_stale_seconds.description: Oldest grant watermark a process still trusts, seconds. Past it (polls keep failing) cached grants are not served and every request reads its own.

acl_watermark_poll_seconds.description: Seconds between each process's reads of the per-org grant watermark (loom.acl_versions): a revoke on one replica is enforced on every other within about this long.

adaptive_thresholds.description: Derive the similarity gates from this embedder's cosine distribution at boot (server/memory/app/embedder_calibration.py). False pins the scalar defaults (tuned for text-embedding-3-small) — re-bench after an embedder change. Fake embedders and probe failures always use the scalars.

allow_insecure.description: True lets a non-loopback bind start with auth off, MCP open mode, open self-signup outside trust-network, the dev signing secret or a weak root, gateway or end-user key. Only for a port others cannot reach.

anthropic_base_url.description: Anthropic's API root (the Messages API is <root>/v1/messages): point it at a gateway in front of Anthropic. Off the default, the key also goes as a bearer, the scheme gateways take.

assistant_answer_ceiling_usd.description: USD charged for an answer cut before LibreChat reported its usage (a disconnect, a timeout) or on a model with no price, so no answer is free.

assistant_answer_ttl_s.description: Seconds one assistant answer may run, and how long its delegated token lives.

assistant_budget_share.description: The share of a namespace's daily model cost cap the assistant may spend, so questions cannot spend what extraction and the conflict resolver need.

assistant_concurrent_answers.description: Answers one web process runs at once per namespace (a replica runs its web workers' count times this); bounds how far answers that each passed the cap check can overshoot it.

assistant_librechat_url.description: LibreChat's internal address (http://librechat:3080), reachable only from Loom. "" = no assistant: no service setup at boot.

assistant_model.description: The assistant agent's model, which LibreChat runs on its own Anthropic key and Loom writes into the agent definition at boot. "" = the definition's own (integrations/librechat/agent.yaml), not llm_model.

assistant_service_email.description: Email of the LibreChat service user that owns the agent, read once, when the first boot writes loom.assistant_service; LibreChat sends it no mail.

assistant_setup_retry_s.description: Seconds before a failed assistant setup is tried again; each next failure doubles the wait, up to 16 times as long (docs/architecture/assistant.md#deployment).

audit_checkpoint_grace_seconds.description: Seconds after a window closes before it is sealed.

audit_checkpoint_max_seal_per_pass.description: Most windows one pass seals; a backlog is sealed over later passes.

audit_checkpoint_verify_windows.description: Most recent sealed windows recounted every pass (at least 1).

audit_checkpoint_window_seconds.description: Length, seconds, of one audit window. Each closed window is sealed as a chained checkpoint once `audit_checkpoint_grace_seconds` old, and the last `audit_checkpoint_verify_windows` are recounted every pass: a short recount is a deletion, which per-row hashes cannot see.

audit_verifier_enabled.description: Periodic re-hash of audit rows; a mismatch writes `audit.tamper_detected`. Per-row detection, not a hash chain (see server/observability/audit.py).

audit_verifier_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between audit verifier passes (row re-hash and checkpoint sealing).

audit_verify_max_rows_per_pass.description: Most audit rows one verifier pass checks; past it the newest go unchecked and the pass says so.

auth_attempts_concurrency.description: Sign-ins, sign-ups and workload-token exchanges one process counts at once (each costs ClickHouse statements, a sign-in a password hash); past it a caller waits up to a second, then gets 429 (an exchange 503), so a burst cannot take the shared connection pool.

auth_machine_discovery_ttl_s.description: Seconds a machine issuer's discovery document (its JWKS URL) is cached.

auth_oidc_discovery_ttl_s.description: Seconds the identity provider's OpenID configuration is cached.

auth_required.description: True: every operation requires a valid bearer JWT. False (laptop demos only): missing tokens are not rejected and the SPA synthesizes a local identity. identity_provider=single-user forces auth off regardless.

background_workers.description: Which processes run the WorkerSupervisor: auto = the one process of the deployment holding the `workers_supervisor` lease in ClickHouse (server/workers/leader.py), and none outside the deployment (no LOOM_DEPLOYMENT); on = always; off = never (a pure web replica).

bind_host.description: The address Loom is reachable on: `loom serve` and `make server` bind it; in a container (which listens on all its interfaces) it is the address the port is published on. Anything but loopback turns on the startup checks in the deployment guide's "Proxy and TLS" section.

blacklist_cache_ttl_seconds.description: Seconds after which the blacklist cache reloads regardless of the version watermark.

blacklist_version_check_interval_seconds.description: Blacklist cache invalidation: in-process invalidate_cache(), a one-row CH version watermark (loom.blacklist_version) polled at most every check interval (bounds cross-replica lag), and a hard TTL backstop. No Redis.

boot_migrate.description: Apply pending migrations at boot. Set False for any server started from a branch against a shared service, or it applies unmerged migrations.

boot_migrate_lease_ttl_s.description: Seconds after which the boot migration lease's holder, once it stops renewing, is replaced.

boot_migrate_lease_wait_s.description: Seconds a contender waits for the holder before boot fails (exit 1, the container restarts); also how long a booting process waits for the provider configuration lock (a sibling's rebuild step may hold it).

boot_warmup_timeout_s.description: Seconds boot waits for the first load of the tracker registry and the runtime overrides, and the first publish of the dashboard bundle, before it serves; readiness stays false until the first two load.

budget_violation_audit_burst.description: Violations per window that still write their own row before the rest are folded into the next: a short burst stays visible, a storm costs at most this many inserts a minute per (op, org, namespace).

budget_violation_audit_interval_s.description: At most one `budget.violated` audit row per op per this many seconds (the row carries `suppressed_since_last`). 0 = a row per violation.

build_commit.description: Deployed git commit, stamped at image build (ARG LOOM_BUILD_COMMIT) and shown in /v1/health. Empty in a source run.

bulk_conflict_check_concurrency.description: Bulk-path conflict checks run at once (at least 1).

bulk_conflict_check_max_entries.description: Entries per bulk call that get the conflict check; later entries are written unchecked and counted. 0 = none are checked. memory.import checks every entry whatever this says.

calibration_refresh_seconds.description: Seconds between each replica's re-read of the shared calibration (loom.embedder_calibration), so every replica serves the same gates.

cell.description: This cell's name (1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9, '-') behind a router, "" = not a cell; set, the process serves only while its cell's rows accept it (docs/architecture/cells.md).

cell_router_timeout_s.description: Seconds a whole placement call to the router may take before the request answers 503.

cell_router_url.description: The router's base URL a cell calls to place a new org; "" = none: in `enforced`, a new org answers 503.

ch_analysis_max_concurrent.description: Statements the analyst user runs at once across every org and replica.

ch_analysis_max_concurrent_per_org.description: Statements one org runs at once on one replica; past it a call answers RATE_LIMITED.

ch_analysis_max_execution_s.description: Seconds one insights.query statement may run.

ch_analysis_max_memory_bytes.description: Bytes of memory one statement may use.

ch_analysis_max_result_bytes.description: Bytes of result one statement may return; past it the statement fails (422).

ch_analysis_max_result_rows.description: Rows one statement returns at most; a longer result comes back cut, marked truncated.

ch_analysis_max_rows_to_read.description: Rows one statement may scan; past it the statement fails (422), never a partial answer.

ch_analysis_max_threads.description: Threads one statement may use (pinned as a MAX, so a statement cannot take the host).

ch_analysis_probe_interval_s.description: Seconds between two probes of the analyst user in each web process; a problem an admin fixes, or a repair a write makes, shows within one interval.

ch_batched_insert_background_wait_max_ms.description: Longest wait, ms, of the usage-event flusher's ticks and shutdown drain and the write-mark timer's flush, which no request waits on.

ch_batched_insert_wait_max_ms.description: Longest wait, ms, of a batched or waited async insert a request waits on; it holds a pooled connection meanwhile.

ch_batched_insert_wait_min_ms.description: Shortest wait, ms, of a batched or waited async insert: what a lone insert waits when writes are sparse; capped at ch_batched_insert_wait_max_ms (or the background bound).

ch_batched_inserts.description: Batch the inserts written on every request into shared parts; false commits them, and the waited async inserts keep their bounds (docs/architecture/clickhouse.md#batched-inserts).

ch_caller_shaped_max_execution_s.description: Seconds one caller-shaped read may run (the read class default); 0 = no ceiling, so the loom_reader profile's cap applies.

ch_caller_shaped_max_memory_bytes.description: Bytes of memory one caller-shaped read may use; 0 = no ceiling, so the loom_reader profile's cap applies.

ch_caller_shaped_max_rows_to_read.description: Rows one caller-shaped read may scan; past it the read fails (422), never a partial answer. 0 = no ceiling, so the loom_reader profile's cap applies.

ch_capture_statements.description: A file path: append one JSON line (`digest`, `sql`) per executed statement, to collect the shapes an acceptance run executes for the analyzer corpus. '' = off; never set it in production.

ch_cluster.description: The cluster `clusterAllReplicas` reads to find a stopped Loom process's queries on every node (`default` on ClickHouse Cloud). A server without it answers for itself; '' reads only the connected server.

ch_database.description: The database Loom's schema lives in: every table, view and the migrations ledger, and the connection's default database. Statements are written against `loom` and name this database where they reach ClickHouse (server/core/ch_names.py); KeeperMap paths move with it. Set it before the first migration: while a schema is in `loom`, a server pointed at a name that does not exist, or holds tables but no Loom ledger, refuses to start (create it empty to start a second schema). A letter or `_`, then letters, digits, `_` and `-`; never `default`, `system`, `information_schema`, or a table or alias name the schema uses. Read once at startup.

ch_host.description: Host name of the ClickHouse server Loom stores everything in.

ch_keepalive_timeout.description: Seconds an idle pooled connection is kept. Must stay BELOW the Cloud load balancer's idle cutoff (8 s) so loom closes first: a peer-closed pooled TLS connection is never reaped under uvloop (`LOOM_UVICORN_LOOP=uvloop`).

ch_log_comment_statement_digest.description: Append `sql:<shape12> <first 200 chars>` of each statement to its `log_comment` ("<op> <request_id>"), so query_log rows group by shape. A statement that carries a secret, or one run as the analyst, gets its shape alone. Off by default: readers that split log_comment on spaces gain tokens.

ch_pool_maxsize.description: HTTP connection pool size: request concurrency plus 3 x the batched-insert bound (inserts a second x wait / 1000; docs/architecture/clickhouse.md#batched-inserts).

ch_pool_wait_ms.description: Max wait, ms, for a pool slot before failing fast with 503 OVERLOADED. 0 = no slot gate.

ch_port.description: ClickHouse HTTP port; 8443 (the Cloud HTTPS port) turns TLS on when `ch_secure` is unset.

ch_read_your_writes.description: A point lookup that MISSES right after a write (get after set, verify, update_by_id, delete) re-reads once with select_sequential_consistency=1. Costs only on a miss; a no-op on single-node MergeTree.

ch_read_your_writes_window_s.description: memory.search on a namespace this process wrote within this many seconds reads with select_sequential_consistency from the start. 0 = off (the empty-pool retry remains the backstop).

ch_reader_user.description: ClickHouse user the caller-shaped reads run as, with `ch_password`; the shipped config defines `loom_reader` (SELECT only). Empty = `ch_user`.

ch_replica_bound_retries.description: Fresh connections a statement tries after a replica-bound error (a replica that lost its Keeper session, a replica's read-only table). Behind a load balancer one reconnect can land on the replica that just failed, so a single retry is not enough.

ch_secure.description: Connect over HTTPS. Unset infers TLS from the port (8443 on, anything else off).

ch_settings_by_traffic_class.description: JSON map {traffic class: ClickHouse settings} applied by `server.core.ch.statement_settings` to every read (an explicit per-call setting wins). `priority`: 1 served first, larger waits, 0 opts out; `max_threads` caps CPU per statement. Neither changes the rows returned. `background` (workers, operator CLIs) bypasses the filesystem cache on a miss so a backfill scan does not evict interactive data.

ch_telemetry_database.description: The database the telemetry Loom derives from its own tables lives in (`sli_minute`), outside the schema so a reader can be granted it alone. A schema outside `loom` names its own: two schemas never share one.

ch_timeout_ddl_s.description: Deadline, seconds, for DDL statements (CREATE, ALTER, DROP); 0 = no bound.

ch_timeout_read_s.description: Deadline, seconds, for read statements, applied as `max_execution_time` and as a client-side bound that frees the pool slot. 0 = no bound for reads.

ch_timeout_write_s.description: Deadline, seconds, for INSERT and UPDATE statements; 0 = no bound.

ch_user.description: User name the server connects to ClickHouse as.

clickstack_database.description: The database ClickStack's OTel tables (HyperDX's) live in, on the same ClickHouse service: where `otel_exporter = "ch"` writes spans, logs and metrics, and where the erasure cascade deletes a user's rows with ALTER TABLE DELETE. "" = the `default` database for the exporter, and no erasure cascade.

clickstack_user_id_keys.description: Comma-separated OTel Map attribute keys holding user_id, ORed in the delete.

code_ask_cache_max_age_days.description: A cached code.ask answer older than this many days is a miss (checked and tombstoned at read time; no table TTL). 0 = no bound.

code_ask_cache_threshold.description: The code.ask answer cache's hit cosine. 0 = the per-embedding-model table in code/app/answers.py; a value in (0, 1] pins one threshold for every model.

code_ask_llm_cache.description: code.ask's pre-synthesis LLM calls (identifier proposal, HyDE, concept legs) read the per-namespace exact-prompt response cache; no_cache or a traffic class with llm_cache off bypasses it.

code_ask_llm_model.description: code.ask synthesis. Answers are memoized fleet-wide, so a stronger model costs once per unique question.

code_ask_memory_namespace.description: The memory namespace code.ask fuses decision/rationale memories (the "why") from into its answer; empty = no enrichment, never guessed.

code_ask_negative_cache_ttl_s.description: Seconds an abstain stays cached for its exact normalised question under the index head it abstained at. 0 = off.

code_ask_token_budget.description: Retrieval context (tokens) code.ask hands to synthesis when the caller passes no token_budget.

code_backport_gaps_budget_s.description: Seconds after which a backport-gaps pass stops starting fixes.

code_backport_gaps_days.description: Days back of backport-labelled trunk PRs a backport-gaps pass considers.

code_backport_gaps_enabled.description: Nightly pass: runs `code.backport_gap(exact, history)` for every trunk PR of the last `code_backport_gaps_days` labelled for backport and writes one row per release branch into loom.code_backport_gaps. Paced one fix per `code_backport_gaps_pace_s`, at most `code_backport_gaps_prs_per_pass` a night, stalest first, stopping at `code_backport_gaps_budget_s`; settled fixes are skipped. Off = nothing written; the read op serves the table.

code_backport_gaps_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between backport-gaps passes; the read op reports the table stale past twice this.

code_backport_gaps_max_pass_seconds.description: A backport-gaps pass's hard deadline (seconds) under the worker supervisor.

code_backport_gaps_pace_s.description: Seconds a backport-gaps pass pauses between two fixes.

code_backport_gaps_prs_per_pass.description: Max fixes a backport-gaps pass checks, stalest first.

code_backport_history_budget_ms.description: Milliseconds the history stage of the backport-gap check may run: one grep per path and a few `-S` reads per undecided branch.

code_backport_patch_budget_ms.description: Milliseconds the hunk-level stage of the backport-gap check may run: one chunk read per branch, all at once.

code_backport_presence_budget_ms.description: Milliseconds the presence stage of the backport-gap check may run.

code_bisect_dupcheck_timeout_s.description: The dupcheck's budget inside a bisect, from the call's start; it runs beside the resolve, the scan and the fusion reads and is awaited only before the ranking stages. Past it the bisect answers without it (`dupcheck_fix.status: timeout`).

code_bisect_fix_blame_budget_s.description: Seconds the fix-blame stage of code.bisect_candidates may run.

code_bisect_history_days.description: Days of the repo's own PR history bisect reads back from the window's end when there is no tracker (or no changed files) and no `after`.

code_bisect_llm_rerank_model.description: code.bisect_candidates' one-call rerank of the fused top 20.

code_bisect_lookback_minors.description: Minor releases searched below the failing one when the report names no clean one.

code_bisect_rerank_timeout_s.description: The rerank's wall budget (seconds); a timeout keeps the fused order.

code_bisect_wide_days.description: The wide read's merge-time window (days) with no release named.

code_bisect_window_days.description: Merge-time window (days) for a report naming no release.

code_blame_cache_ttl_s.description: Seconds code.blame_range keeps a blame text, a window graph or a branch point per key.

code_blame_graph_timeout_s.description: Seconds the commit-graph read of code.blame_range may run.

code_blame_introduced_diff_timeout_s.description: Seconds one `git diff` of the introduced-by test may run.

code_blame_introduced_max_diff_calls.description: Most candidates the introduced-by diff test checks per request, blamed ones first, then ledger-only ones by recency.

code_blame_max_graph_commits.description: Most commits code.blame_range's window graph reads; a longer history is a caller asking for everything, which blame cannot rank.

code_blame_timeout_s.description: Seconds one `git blame` of code.blame_range may run.

code_bootstrap_backoff_max_s.description: Longest wait, in seconds, before a mirror fetches again for a commit no fetch has brought.

code_bootstrap_clone_timeout_s.description: Seconds a bare clone may take before the worker gives up for the pass and retries next pass.

code_bootstrap_embed_breaker_hold_s.description: After a slice in which the provider answered nothing, the next slices store stubs (the recovery worker fills them) rather than pay a timeout per file; the breaker closes by itself after the hold.

code_bootstrap_files_per_pass.description: Files indexed per pass while a new entry's initial index builds; the cursor persists in code_index_state (400 ≈ 1 min at the live rate).

code_bootstrap_mirror_refresh_s.description: Seconds after a successful mirror fetch before another read may start one.

code_bootstrap_mirror_retry_s.description: Seconds after a failed mirror clone or fetch before it is tried again; a commit no fetch has brought waits this, doubled per fetch.

code_bot_authors.description: Comma-separated GitHub logins of autonomous agents that author pull requests or issues in the indexed repositories, beyond the generic bots (dependabot, github-actions, …). They are never suggested as owners, their names are not tracker entities, and bisect ignores the lines they sign.

code_callers_candidate_min_confidence.description: The floor below which a declined site code.callers / code.callees return is counted, not returned; a request may pass `candidate_min_confidence`.

code_callers_max_distinct_seeds.description: code.callers/callees: a bare name with more distinct definitions than this returns `ambiguous` + candidates instead of walking them all.

code_chunk_max_chars.description: Chunking: whole AST units; functions larger than this split at top-level statement boundaries, each piece re-prefixed with the signature header.

code_citations_git_budget_s.description: Seconds of git time code.verify_citations may spend per request.

code_citations_git_call_cap.description: Most git subprocesses code.verify_citations may start per request.

code_citations_git_call_timeout_s.description: Seconds one git call of code.verify_citations may run, within its request budget.

code_closure_repair_enabled.description: Closure repair: a bare function name the commit added with exactly ONE live definition repo-wide binds its `unresolved` sites at 0.6 without re-parsing; several definitions leave them declined. Capped per commit.

code_closure_repair_max_names.description: Added and removed names per commit closure repair considers; the rest are skipped.

code_closure_repair_max_sites.description: Unresolved call sites closure repair reads per commit for the names it binds.

code_compact_after_bulk_rows.description: A bulk `loom code` pass that wrote at least this many chunk rows ends by compacting the prefix/twin vector tables past code_compact_min_ratio. 0 = off; loom.code_chunks is compacted only by the CLI.

code_compact_min_ratio.description: Copies per key (active rows / distinct keys) at which a code vector table is OPTIMIZE ... FINAL'd.

code_compaction_timeout_s.description: Seconds a code-table compaction waits for its OPTIMIZE to finish.

code_context_description_enabled.description: Contextual-embedding one-liner per chunk, inline on the per-merge path; falls back to structural-only on any LLM failure.

code_context_description_prompt.description: Shape of the embedded chunk description: `oneliner` (what the code does) or `questions` (file card + chunk → what it does and the questions it answers). Changing it re-texts new rows only.

code_conventions_diff_max_bytes.description: Max bytes of a PR patch code.conventions reads from the mirror; a longer patch is cut at a file boundary and flagged `diff_truncated`.

code_conventions_diff_timeout_s.description: Seconds the git diff behind code.conventions may run.

code_conventions_wide_caller_dirs.description: A touched function is "widely called" when its hop-1 callers span more than this many `src/<dir>` directories (rule wide_callers_untested).

code_corpus_stats_max_terms.description: Max terms whose df the per-process cache holds; the oldest goes first.

code_corpus_stats_ttl_s.description: Seconds the BM25 corpus statistics (term df, chunk count, mean length) are cached per process; 0 = no cache. Bounded by `code_corpus_stats_max_terms`, oldest out.

code_coverage_check_pattern.description: Check names (a LIKE pattern) whose runs carry per-test coverage.

code_coverage_control_symbol.description: Positive-control symbol code.test_home / code.coverage_claim grep for (one every test suite of the repository names); empty makes every claim `unknown`.

code_coverage_control_ttl_s.description: Seconds the coverage control's answer is kept per (org, namespace). The control is one read per namespace, not one per claim. The brief builder makes a claim per touched function, and each would re-run the same `arrayJoin` grep over the tests tree (176 MB a statement on the ClickHouse namespace). Its answer — is the tests corpus measurable from here — holds for a namespace across a brief, so it is kept, in this process only.

code_coverage_import_enabled.description: Import per-test line coverage from an instrumented CI run into the test map (`method='coverage'`) and the per-file executed lines (`code_coverage_files`). Off by default; `loom code coverage-import` runs one import by hand whatever this says.

code_coverage_import_max_pass_seconds.description: Seconds one coverage import pass may run before the supervisor abandons it.

code_coverage_namespaces.description: Namespaces (CSV) whose repository the source's runs cover; every other namespace is skipped.

code_coverage_notify_enabled.description: Coverage watches: post one code.coverage.ready event on the watcher's task inbox once every index tier covers a watched commit. A pass with no pending watch is one read of an empty table.

code_coverage_notify_idle_interval_secon.description: Seconds between coverage-notify passes that found no pending watch.

code_coverage_notify_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between coverage-notify passes while watches are pending.

code_coverage_run_window_hours.description: Jobs of one run start within this many hours of its newest job.

code_coverage_shards.description: The run's coverage is read in this many slices by file hash, two statements per slice. One slice must fit the source server's per-query memory, and a source with a per-statement-shape hourly quota (a public playground allows 100) must take a whole import plus a retry: a nightly run read in 16 slices is 16 statements of each shape.

code_coverage_source_connect_timeout_s.description: Seconds the coverage import waits to connect to the source endpoint.

code_coverage_source_database.description: Database of the coverage source's tables.

code_coverage_source_timeout_s.description: Seconds one source query may take before the import stops (no rows are tombstoned by an import that did not finish).

code_coverage_source_url.description: ClickHouse HTTP endpoint holding the coverage tables (`checks_coverage_lines`, `checks`); "" = no source, the import is a no-op.

code_coverage_source_user.description: User the coverage import signs in to the source endpoint as.

code_coverage_specific_max_tests.description: A line executed by more tests than this names none of them (shared plumbing every query runs); a test-map row needs a line under the cap.

code_crossref_enabled.description: SQL <-> C++ crossref (code_test_map from registrations and test queries) for each C++ entry whose git_head moved since its last run.

code_describe_concurrency.description: A file's chunk descriptions in flight at once; 1 = serial.

code_egress_connect_timeout_s.description: Seconds a repository job's egress tunnel waits to connect to its upstream host.

code_egress_idle_timeout_s.description: Seconds a repository job's egress tunnel may move no byte before it is closed.

code_egress_slot_wait_s.description: Seconds a repository job's connection waits for a free egress tunnel slot.

code_embed_max_attempts.description: Embed attempts per stub before it is poisoned (`embed_failed_at` set) and skipped.

code_embed_recovery_batch.description: Stub keys the recovery scan takes per repo per pass (also texts per embed call); raise it to onboard large repositories faster.

code_embed_recovery_chain_budget_s.description: Seconds one embed-recovery pass may spend chaining scans before it stops for the next pass.

code_embed_recovery_full_scan_seconds.description: The pending scan reads above a version watermark; once per this many seconds it scans from version 0 to catch late rows. 0 = always from 0.

code_embed_recovery_idle_interval_second.description: Sleep after a code embed-recovery pass that found no pending stub; `code_embed_recovery_interval_seconds` resumes once a pass writes a row.

code_embed_recovery_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between recovery passes while stubs are pending.

code_enrich_timeout_s.description: Seconds one enrichment of a code result may take before it is left empty.

code_entry_lock_wait_s.description: A full pass waits this long for a delta on its entry (past any delta's harness timeout).

code_extractor_rechunk_concurrency.description: Files a re-chunk re-derives at once. A re-derive waits mostly on its ClickHouse reads and writes, so raising this shortens a heal roughly in proportion, at that much more concurrent load on the cluster.

code_extractor_rechunk_enabled.description: When the recorded parser/chunker/grammar stamp differs from the running process, re-chunk the namespace in paced batches per ingest pass. A first observation is recorded, never acted on.

code_extractor_rechunk_per_pass.description: Live paths re-chunked per ingest pass while the stamp differs.

code_fan_in_prior_cap.description: Cap of code.search's fan-in rank prior: score *= 1 + cap * log1p(fan_in) / log1p(max fan_in in the pool); skipped under test intent and on noise paths; inert without the stats. 0 = off.

code_fetch_stale_after_seconds.description: as_of.stale is also true when the mirror has not fetched for this many seconds (lag is counted against the local mirror). 0 = off.

code_fork_upstream_budget_s.description: Seconds the lookup of a repository's fork upstream may take.

code_fork_upstream_cache_ttl_s.description: Seconds a repository's known fork upstreams are cached.

code_fork_upstream_miss_ttl_s.description: Seconds a failed fork-upstream lookup is remembered as "not a known fork".

code_fusion_signals.description: Post-fusion rank priors in code.search (path-noise penalty, query↔path stem affinity, file coherence), applied after RRF and before the outcome boost. Kill switch.

code_gh_items_backfill_days.description: Days back the first mirror pass (and `loom code` with no start date) reads.

code_gh_items_enabled.description: Keep loom.code_gh_items current: every issue and PR updated since the last pass via /issues; the first pass reaches back backfill_days. Skipped anonymously.

code_gh_items_head_fill_batch.description: Open-PR rows per pass whose head_sha / base_sha / files the PR-history worker fills from the mirror; rows the mirror lacks fall back to GitHub (`code_gh_items_head_github_batch`).

code_gh_items_head_github_batch.description: GitHub `GET /pulls/N` calls per pass for open PRs the mirror lacks; 0 = the mirror path only.

code_git_branch.description: The scalar entry's branch: the one the ingest worker fetches and indexes.

code_git_dir.description: Bare clone the ingest worker fetches into (created by `loom code init`). Empty = derived from code_repo: `var/code_repos/<name>.git`.

code_git_extra_branches.description: Comma-separated fnmatch globs of extra remote branches the mirror fetches besides the configured one (`release/*` = release branches, `backport/*` = backport staging). Refs are never pruned. Empty = the configured branch only.

code_git_fetch_ledger_merges.description: Fetch ledger merge commits no branch reaches by sha and pin them under refs/loom/merges/<sha>: one ledger page and at most `code_git_ledger_merge_batch` shas per entry per pass; the cursor wraps. Off = branches only.

code_git_fetch_pr_heads.description: The mirror carries `refs/pull/N/head` for every PR the ledger holds OPEN (refetched when the tip moves, never pruned), so pre-merge reads diff the PR's own head. Only open heads: fetching every PR head is too costly. Per-entry `git_fetch_pr_heads` overrides. Off = the overlay reports `head_not_in_mirror`.

code_git_fetch_timeout_s.description: Seconds one fetch, full-tree `ls-tree`, forced checkout or whole-range diff may run; the first fetch after a shallow clone of a large repository can exceed ten minutes.

code_git_ledger_merge_batch.description: Missing ledger merge shas fetched per entry per pass (40 take about 8.5 s).

code_git_ledger_merge_page.description: Ledger merge rows checked for a missing sha per entry per pass.

code_git_pr_head_batch.description: Max PR heads fetched per shared mirror per ingest pass.

code_git_remote.description: The scalar entry's fetch remote; empty = `https://github.com/<owner>/<name>.git`.

code_git_timeout_s.description: Seconds one git command on a mirror may run (log, show, rev-parse).

code_graph_stats_enabled.description: Weekly graph statistics: PageRank, degrees, test_map rebuild.

code_graph_stats_max_pass_seconds.description: A graph-statistics pass's deadline (seconds); a pass past it is cancelled and counted a failure.

code_graph_stats_unit_risk_budget_s.description: Seconds from the start of a graph-statistics pass during which its unit-risk leg may schedule rounds; past it the pass succeeds with `unit_risk_partial: true` and the next resumes. Must stay under `code_graph_stats_max_pass_seconds`.

code_history_clone_on_read.description: Whether a history read (blame_range, bisect, first_build, lesson checks) on a host without a repository's mirror clones it there in the background. On: every serving host keeps its own full copy of every mirror it is asked about. Off: such a host answers `no_git_mirror` and only the worker's host clones.

code_host_islands.description: Shell inside CI/build files (Actions `run:`, GitLab `script:`, Dockerfile `RUN`, Makefile recipes, Jenkinsfile `sh`) is parsed for facets, script `includes` edges and SQL; jobs, targets and stages become symbols, and extensionless Dockerfile / Makefile / Jenkinsfile index as config. Needs a `--paths-file` backfill.

code_ingest_denylist_builtin.description: True applies the built-in generated, minified and vendored ingest rules (code/app/index/denylist.py), which match 0.19% of rows. The `exclude` globs (CSV here, a list per repo entry) and the repo-local ignore file are always honoured.

code_ingest_dependents_concurrency.description: Dependents re-extracted at once; the batch is bound by ClickHouse read throughput, so more is not faster.

code_ingest_dependents_enabled.description: After a commit, re-extract edges only on untouched files whose call sites or edges reference symbols it added, removed or tombstoned (or, opt-in, that include a touched header). Capped per commit; overflow drains through reconcile. A replay closed every gap at 20% of the ingest wall.

code_ingest_dependents_max_files.description: Dependent files re-extracted per commit; the overflow queues for reconcile.

code_ingest_dependents_pending_max.description: Size cap of the dependents re-extraction overflow queue; paths past it are dropped and counted.

code_ingest_enabled.description: Per-merge fast tier: git-poll → diff → re-chunk/re-embed changed files → tree-sitter symbols/edges → context pack → advance watermark.

code_ingest_exclude.description: CSV of path globs never indexed (the scalar entry's `exclude`).

code_ingest_ignore_file.description: Name of the repo-local ignore file whose patterns are never indexed.

code_ingest_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between fast-tier ingest passes; extra-branch fetches of a shared mirror are spaced by 0.9 of it (at least 30 s).

code_ingest_lanes.description: Entries whose commits ingest side by side in the commit phase. Each entry's own commits stay one at a time, oldest first (the watermark contract); a lane waits on ClickHouse round trips, not on its capacity, so lanes add throughput. 1 = one commit at a time across all entries.

code_ingest_live_paths_ttl_s.description: Seconds an ingesting process caches the namespace's live path set (the import-resolution oracle); files it writes join at once.

code_ingest_max_commits_per_pass.description: Commits past the watermark one pass reads; later ones wait for the next pass.

code_ingest_max_file_bytes.description: Files above this size are recorded (index_error) and not chunked. 0 = no cap.

code_ingest_max_files_per_commit.description: Changed files indexed per commit; past it the rest are skipped with a warning and heal on the next backfill.

code_ingest_max_pass_seconds.description: The ingest pass's own deadline (seconds), kept at the supervisor's cap; `code_ingest_pass_budget_fraction` keeps a pass under it.

code_ingest_pass_budget_fraction.description: Fraction of the deadline after which the pass stops STARTING units, finishes the in-flight round, saves cursors and returns `partial: true`.

code_ingest_round_files.description: Files per round in the walk, the bootstrap slice and a commit's file list; a round prefetches its per-file resolution reads in two statements. 0 = per-file reads.

code_ingest_round_model_concurrency.description: Model calls one round runs at once.

code_ingest_round_write_rows.description: Buffered rows at which an ingest round writes a table early. A round writes one INSERT per table, flushed when a read could see the rows, at this row count, or at round end.

code_ingest_seconds_per_file.description: Prior ingest cost per changed file (seconds), refined by observation. A commit predicted to overrun the pass deadline is not started unless it is the first of its pass.

code_ingest_sibling_text_ttl_s.description: Seconds the ingest keeps a sibling-text answer (a manifest, a listing, a config, a barrel).

code_ingest_slice_share.description: Share of the commit phase one oversized commit may take per pass while other entries wait (it is sliced across passes).

code_ingest_walk_budget_share.description: Share of the ingest pass budget (`code_ingest_pass_budget_fraction` of the deadline) the commit phase leaves to the walk (reconcile heal, extractor re-chunk). 0 = commits may take it all.

code_intel_enabled.description: Master kill switch, checked at the top of every code.* handler but the retirement (code.repo.remove), which only deletes.

code_jit_risk_max_age_days.description: Days after which a fit is served as `scored_stale` / `fit_stale`.

code_jit_risk_refit_interval_s.description: Seconds after which the weekly pass refits the jit-risk model.

code_jit_risk_window_months.description: Months of merged PRs the JIT risk model's fit reads.

code_link_revise_model.description: The code-link `revise` judge: does a memory's claim still hold for its code's new text.

code_merge_shas_log_timeout_s.description: Seconds the mirror's git log may run when it searches for merge commits.

code_merge_shas_max_log_commits.description: Most commits the mirror's git log prints when it searches for merge commits.

code_message_grep_error_codes_ttl_s.description: Seconds a repository's error-code table is cached for message search.

code_mirror_clone_wait_s.description: The longest a history read waits for a clone it started; less when its op's budget is.

code_mirror_fetch_interval_s.description: Seconds between this host's fetches of its mirrors and sweeps of the mirrors, checkouts and lock files no active entry names. A round fetches only the branch tips, open PR heads and ledger merges the leader's pass recorded in ClickHouse that the mirror lacks: nothing when it is current. 0 = no fetch loop and no sweep.

code_mirror_gc_interval_h.description: Hours between `git gc` runs of each mirror on this host (low CPU and IO priority, only with room for a second copy plus `code_mirror_gc_margin_gb`). 0 = never.

code_mirror_gc_margin_gb.description: Free disk, in GB, a mirror's gc must leave beyond the mirror's own size; without it the gc waits another interval.

code_mirror_gc_timeout_s.description: Seconds one `git gc` of a mirror may run.

code_mirror_warmup.description: Every serving process clones the configured entries' mirrors it lacks at boot, in the background (code/app/index/mirrors.py): a history read answers `no_git_mirror: cloning <entry>` until its mirror is there. A full bare clone per host, again on every new disk: keep code_repos_root on a volume that outlives a rollout. Off: a mirror is cloned only when a read asks for it.

code_mirror_warmup_concurrency.description: Clones the warm-up runs at once on one host (each after a random wait), so N replicas starting together do not all clone from the remote at once.

code_mirror_warmup_retry_s.description: Seconds before a failed warm-up clone of a mirror is tried again.

code_namespace.description: The scalar entry's code namespace, used by a code.* request or `loom code` command that names none; empty = the request must name one.

code_org.description: The scalar repository entry's loom org; empty is never a default for a code.* request, which then must name its own.

code_org_readable.description: True lets every authenticated principal of the org read every configured code namespace (right for public or org-internal repos); false leaves reads to the namespace's own visibility and grants. Writes stay grant-driven. Per-entry "org_readable" in LOOM_CODE_REPOS_JSON.

code_parse_memory_mb.description: Address space (MB) one tree-sitter parse may take; one runs at a time per server process, which holds up to this plus about 170 MB for it. Past it the file is chunks without symbols.

code_parse_timeout_s.description: CPU seconds a tree-sitter parse may take, a tenth of them at a stretch between reads or after the last; a PR overlay waits up to this long past its window.

code_path_prefixes.description: CSV path prefixes of the scalar entry that are indexed; everything else is skipped. Empty = the whole tree (the ingest denylist still applies).

code_pr_backfill_months.description: Months of merged PRs `loom code backfill-prs` (and a cold worker) fetch; matches the churn window in code/app/risk.py.

code_pr_check_closed_days.description: Days back code.pr_check reads PRs closed without a merge.

code_pr_check_duplicate_threshold.description: Verdict: `duplicate_of` when a candidate's heuristic score reaches the duplicate line (a closed-unmerged PR caps at related), `related` at the related line, else `none`. A title alone never reaches duplicate.

code_pr_check_mass_files.description: Files above which a code.pr_check candidate is a mass change, whose files do not vote.

code_pr_check_merged_days.description: Days back code.pr_check reads merged PRs; older ones do not vote as duplicates.

code_pr_check_related_threshold.description: Score at or above which a candidate is `related`.

code_pr_overlay_cache_ttl_s.description: Seconds a PR overlay (the PR's changed files over its base) is cached; one that left changed files unreached is not.

code_pr_overlay_file_ttl_s.description: Seconds one PR file's parse is kept, so a push that changes one file re-parses that file alone; a PR's next review follows its next push.

code_pr_overlay_parse_window_s.description: Seconds after a PR overlay begins past which it starts no parse; the files it did not reach are counted in `overlay_note` and read by a later request.

code_pr_reviews_enabled.description: Also fetch each merged PR's inline review comments into loom.code_pr_reviews (one request per PR; skipped without a GitHub token).

code_py_sql_islands.description: SQL a Python file runs (database-client call arguments and SQL-looking literals) becomes `statement` symbols, facets (confidence 0.7 with a format hole) and table edges. Off = functions only. Needs a `--paths-file` backfill of the Python tree.

code_ready_embed_coverage.description: Share of embeddable chunks that must carry a vector before a repo is `ready`; below it code.search says "lexical only". Poisoned rows count against it; fixtures unembedded by design do not.

code_reconcile_enabled.description: Content-based reconciliation (code/app/index/reconcile.py): each interval, compare every path's chunk commit with the branch head and re-ingest up to `code_reconcile_heal_per_pass` stale paths.

code_reconcile_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between reconciliation runs per namespace.

code_reconcile_max_commits.description: Max distinct chunk commits a run compares; past it the stale set is a floor (`truncated`).

code_repo.description: The scalar entry's GitHub `owner/name`; empty = no scalar entry, so nothing is indexed until a repository is configured.

code_repo_public.description: The scalar repo entry is public: its namespace registers join_policy=open and discoverable. Per-entry `"public": true` does the same.

code_repos_root.description: Where the code ingest worker clones a self-service entry's bare mirror (one per GitHub repository, shared by its branches).

code_repos_shared_gid.description: Numeric gid of the prepared var/code_repos: mirror and checkout directories in it 2770, locks 0660, server and `loom code` umask 007. Unset: 0700, 0600, the caller's umask.

code_review_brief_mirror_miss_ttl_s.description: Seconds before the review brief reads a mirror again for an object it did not have (the mirror may have fetched it); a hit is kept.

code_review_brief_rationale_paths.description: Changed paths the `rationale` section reads, source paths first; paths past it make `rationale` say `unknown` (`paths_not_read`).

code_review_brief_rationale_rows.description: Decision and constraint rows the `rationale` section serves.

code_review_brief_rationale_tokens.description: The `rationale` section's own token budget; its first row is served even past it.

code_risk_annotations.description: Per-result risk annotations (churn/amp/tested) and one-hop callee context on code.search results; reserves part of the token budget. Kill switch.

code_sandbox_cpu_seconds.description: CPU seconds one process of a sandboxed repository job may use.

code_sandbox_max_file_mb.description: Largest file one process of a sandboxed repository job may write, in MiB (a pack or index.scip).

code_sandbox_max_pids.description: Processes and threads one job may run at once (RLIMIT_NPROC, set inside the job's user namespace, so other jobs and the server do not count; Linux 5.14+, older kernels count the uid's tasks host-wide).

code_sandbox_memory_mb.description: Data memory (heap and private mappings, RLIMIT_DATA) one process of a sandboxed repository job may use, in MiB. Not address space: node reserves far more of that than it uses.

code_sandbox_required.description: Set by deployments that ship the sandbox profiles: a repository job refuses to run rather than run unsandboxed, and /v1/health reports the missing sandbox as an error. False: without the sandbox, jobs fall back to plain processes as "Without the sandbox" in code-index-operations.md says.

code_scip_apply_enabled.description: SCIP delta apply (compiler-grade tier uploaded via code.scip_ingest).

code_scip_checkout_dir.description: The scalar entry's working tree the compiler tiers index; other entries default to a sibling named after their namespace, and an entry's `scip_checkout_dir` wins.

code_scip_clang_jobs.description: scip-clang's parallel jobs in a delta or full run; 0 = half the CPUs the host shows (a container sees the node's). Each job holds a translation unit's AST: a few GiB for a large C++ tree.

code_scip_clang_path.description: The scip-clang binary: a name looked up on PATH, or a path. The image carries it on amd64 only (upstream builds no arm64 Linux binary).

code_scip_delta_enabled.description: C++ compiler-tier per-merge deltas: scip-clang over changed TUs when git_head outruns scip_commit. Needs the configured checkout and a scip-clang binary; CPU-heavy in bursts.

code_scip_delta_file_max_mb.description: Largest compiler-tier delta file the server reads, in MiB; a larger one fails the entry's pass. It bounds the work of an entry's pass and the path text kept (code-index-operations.md).

code_scip_delta_max_nodes.description: Most `{`, `[` and `,` bytes a compiler-tier delta may hold, counted before it is parsed; more fails the entry's pass (sizing: code-index-operations.md).

code_scip_delta_max_tus.description: Max translation units one delta indexes; past it only the changed `.cpp` files are indexed and the header fan-out heals on the next full run.

code_scip_delta_round_max_nodes.description: Most `{`, `[` and `,` bytes one apply round of a compiler-tier delta parses: its memory bound; one value over it fails the pass (code-index-operations.md).

code_scip_delta_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds the C++ delta harness may run before it is killed.

code_scip_full_enabled.description: C++ full re-index: seeds an entry the delta has no watermark for, and re-indexes each entry every `code_scip_full_every_hours` (heals deltas that hit the TU cap). One entry per pass, under its entry lock.

code_scip_full_every_hours.description: Hours between full re-indexes of one entry.

code_scip_full_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between the C++ full re-index's checks for an entry that is due.

code_scip_full_retry_s.description: Seconds before a failed compiler-tier full re-index of an entry is tried again.

code_scip_full_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds the full re-index harness (CMake configure, scip-clang, convert) may run; the checkout move and the apply get 6 h more in the pass deadline.

code_scip_go_bin_dir.description: Directory holding `go` and scip-go when they are not on PATH; empty = PATH only.

code_scip_go_delta_enabled.description: Go compiler-tier deltas: scip-go per touched module of an entry with `scip_producer` "go". Needs the Go toolchain and scip-go (`go install github.com/scip-code/scip-go/cmd/scip-go@v0.2.7`, the image's version).

code_scip_go_delta_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds the Go delta harness may run before it is killed; also the pass deadline.

code_scip_go_jobs.description: Go modules the delta harness builds in parallel (about 4 GB of memory each).

code_scip_go_modcache.description: Root of the Go module caches kept across passes: one per entry beneath it (<root>/<org>/<namespace>), never shared between repositories.

code_scip_go_path.description: The scip-go binary, looked up on PATH or in `code_scip_go_bin_dir`.

code_scip_go_private.description: GOPRIVATE and GONOSUMDB for the Go delta harness: module paths fetched directly, without the proxy or checksum database (a vanity import host). Empty = none.

code_scip_lock_dir.description: Directory of the per-entry lock files every compiler-tier pass on this host takes (`scip.<org>.<namespace>.lock`): a full re-index and a delta never work on one entry at once; different entries run side by side. `loom code entry-lock` takes the same lock.

code_scip_max_part_bytes.description: Max bytes of one code.scip_ingest payload part; a larger part is refused.

code_scip_max_parts.description: Max `total_parts` of one code.scip_ingest upload; more is refused.

code_scip_py_delta_enabled.description: Python compiler-tier deltas: scip-python over an entry with `scip_producer` "python", over the files the window touched (a first run indexes the tree). Needs node and scip-python.

code_scip_py_delta_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds the Python delta harness may run before it is killed.

code_scip_py_heap_mb.description: Node heap size (MiB) given to scip-python; Pyright dies silently at 8 GB.

code_scip_python_path.description: The scip-python binary: a name looked up on PATH, or a path.

code_scip_ts_delta_enabled.description: TypeScript compiler-tier deltas: scip-typescript over an entry with `scip_producer` "typescript" when git_head outruns scip_commit_ts. The worker prepares dependencies with lifecycle scripts disabled; needs Node 22+ and the toolchain from scripts/install-code-toolchains.sh (in the image).

code_scip_ts_delta_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds the TypeScript delta harness may run before it is killed.

code_scip_ts_node_heap_mb.description: Node heap size (MiB) given to scip-typescript.

code_scip_ts_paths.description: Rewrite consumers' tsconfig `paths` from workspace `exports` before indexing an unbuilt checkout; off for a built checkout.

code_scip_typescript_path.description: The scip-typescript binary: a name looked up on PATH, or a path.

code_scip_work_dir.description: Where the C++ harness writes its index and delta (several GB for a full run of a large tree); "" = the system temp dir.

code_search_abstain_card_below.description: A prose question whose nearest file card's cosine is below this abstains `off_domain`; independent of the card leg. 0 = off.

code_search_abstain_confidence_below.description: Calibrated confidence below which a result is flagged `low_calibrated_confidence` (still returned). The deployment sets 0.30.

code_search_bodies_default.description: code.search `bodies` when the request omits it: "auto" fills bodies into the budget; "none" serves handles only.

code_search_card_leg.description: The card leg: file cards are searched by cosine and the top files' chunks join fusion as a capped RRF list (the history leg's shape). No per-request override.

code_search_card_leg_cap.description: Max share of the best two-leg RRF score a card row contributes.

code_search_card_leg_files.description: Files the card leg votes for.

code_search_card_leg_kinds.description: CSV of prose question kinds the card leg votes on; `any` = all.

code_search_card_leg_mode.description: What a voted file contributes: `skeleton` (its class skeletons) or `best_chunk` (its source chunks nearest the query by exact cosine).

code_search_card_leg_units_per_file.description: Skeleton chunks per voted file (the history leg's shape).

code_search_cards_fetch_multiplier.description: Over-fetch multiplier of the file-card leg's codes shortlist once loom.code_summaries carries the codec.

code_search_catalogue_penalty.description: Fusion multiplier for settings-catalogue units (Settings.cpp and kin) on the question kinds `code_search_catalogue_kinds` names; 1.0 = off.

code_search_concept_expand_cap.description: Max share of the best two-leg RRF score a concept unit contributes.

code_search_concept_expand_kinds.description: CSV of prose question kinds the concept leg expands; `any` = all.

code_search_concept_expand_max_terms.description: Identifiers + phrases code.search's concept expansion keeps from the model's answer.

code_search_concept_expand_min_idf.description: Expansion tokens below this BM25 idf are dropped (2.0 ≈ in more than an eighth of chunks).

code_search_concept_expand_model.description: code.search concept expansion: maps a prose, unconstrained question to likely code identifiers — via this model, or `cards` / `cards:<n>` (symbols of the n nearest file cards) — fused as a capped lexical list. "" = off.

code_search_cursor_enabled.description: A computed code.search / code.grep stores its ranked pool (no bodies) in loom.code_search_memo and issues `next_cursor`; the next page is a point read. The pool size is `code_search_cursor_pool`.

code_search_cursor_pool.description: Units kept in a cursor's ranked pool; capped at 200.

code_search_deadline_ms.description: Default code.search request budget (ms) when the request sets no `deadline_ms`; what it cuts (late legs, rerank) makes the answer `partial`. 0 = none.

code_search_fanout_max_namespaces.description: Max namespaces one request fans out to; can only lower the wire cap of 8.

code_search_fanout_timeout_ms.description: Wall deadline (ms) per namespace in a multi-namespace search; a late namespace is dropped and named in `fanout.dropped`.

code_search_file_saturation.description: Per-file saturation: the 2nd, 3rd... unit from one path is multiplied by decay^excess before the cut; a file's best unit never decays. 0 = off. Skipped under path_prefix, symbol routes and test intent.

code_search_history_anchor_max_files.description: Max PR files of a number intent that anchor the ranking (present files stay, absent ones insert at rank 1); a phrase intent never anchors.

code_search_history_max_prs.description: PR rows served in code.search's `history` section (no bodies; inside the token budget).

code_search_history_route.description: History intent: a question about a change is answered from the PR plane as a `history` section. "off" | "number" (explicit issue/PR numbers, point reads) | "on" (also why/when/who-changed phrasings).

code_search_hyde_cap.description: Cap on the hypothetical-answer (HyDE) leg's candidate list, as a multiple of the two-leg top (the history rule).

code_search_hyde_kinds.description: The question kinds the hypothetical answer votes on.

code_search_hyde_max_tokens.description: Tokens the hypothetical-answer (HyDE) passage may run to.

code_search_hyde_model.description: code.search HyDE: writes a hypothetical indexed passage whose embedding runs a second vector list (see code_search_hyde_*). "" = off.

code_search_llm_leg_grace_ms.description: Ms a model-backed leg (HyDE) may run past the last plain leg before it is dropped. 0 = no bound.

code_search_llm_legs_default.description: Default `llm_legs`: `auto` runs the configured model-backed legs; `none` skips them.

code_search_low_risk_from.description: The calibrated confidence from which a code.search result reads `retrieval_risk` "low" (see code_search_medium_risk_from).

code_search_medium_risk_from.description: The calibrated confidence from which a code.search result reads `retrieval_risk` "medium"; below it the result reads "high". Code embeddings score a right hit lower than memory text does: on the conceptual question set every right top 3 scored 0.40–0.63, so the memory plane's 0.55 / 0.75 labelled three in four right answers "high".

code_search_memo_enabled.description: Memoise served code.search responses per (org, namespace, request shape) in loom.code_search_memo and replay within the TTL (route "+memo"); `fresh=true` bypasses it.

code_search_memo_max_payload_bytes.description: Max bytes of a response the memo stores; a larger one is not memoised. 0 = no cap.

code_search_memo_ttl_s.description: Seconds a memoised response, and a cursor's stored pool, stay replayable.

code_search_pattern_max_files.description: A `pattern` admitting more files than this is refused with `pattern_too_broad` and the count (1,500 = 5% of a large namespace's files).

code_search_pr_leg.description: History leg: merged-PR text scored lexically votes for the files each PR touched, as a third RRF list. "off" | "issue" (issue-shaped queries) | "always".

code_search_pr_leg_cap.description: Per-unit cap on code.search's PR leg contribution, as a fraction of the top two-leg fusion score.

code_search_pr_leg_max_files.description: Files of the PRs code.search's PR leg reads that may vote per query.

code_search_pr_leg_min_prs.description: A namespace with fewer live voting PRs than this skips code.search's PR leg.

code_search_pr_leg_path_prefixes.description: Only files under these prefixes (CSV) receive votes from code.search's PR leg; "" = every file.

code_search_pr_leg_pool.description: PRs code.search's PR leg reads per query.

code_search_pr_leg_units_per_file.description: Chunk units a file voted by code.search's PR leg contributes.

code_search_prose_penalty.description: Fusion multiplier for prose files (documentation, release notes, changelogs) unless the query asks for documentation or the search is constrained to paths; 1.0 = off.

code_search_query_max_tokens.description: Long-question trim: past this many lexemes the question is treated as an issue body (template headings stripped, the rarest 32 tokens gate, the first 512 cleaned words embed). Under the cap nothing changes. 0 = off.

code_search_rerank_default.description: Reranker code.search and code.ask use when the request names none (same values as the per-request `rerank`: a builtin or a name in LOOM_RERANK_ENDPOINTS_JSON; rerank="none" turns it off). Empty = no default rerank.

code_search_rerank_excerpt_chars.description: Characters of each candidate shown to the default rerank (path and signature first, then the body head).

code_search_rerank_kinds.description: Prose question kinds the default rerank applies to (`any` = all); symbol-shaped or constrained searches are never default-reranked.

code_search_rerank_top.description: How many fused units the default rerank reads.

code_search_rrf_lexical_weight_responsib.description: Lexical list's RRF weight for a responsibility question (vector = 1.0). 1.0 = equal weights.

code_search_vector_model_default.description: Default vector-leg shortlist label (`prefix:<dim>:<served model>`, listed in code_search_vector_models and code_vector_tables), rescored by the served vectors. Needs code_search_vector_shortlist > 0; an empty shortlist falls back to the full scan. Empty = off.

code_search_vector_models.description: CSV of vector-model specs a request may name as `vector_model` (e.g. "prefix:512:text-embedding-3-large"); only the vector leg switches. Empty = the override is refused.

code_search_vector_shortlist.description: With a vector_model set and this > 0, the second model's top-N ids are rescored by exact cosine on the served vectors. 0 = its own distances rank. Per-request CodeSearchInput.vector_shortlist.

code_self_service_enabled.description: Repositories added from the Repositories page (loom.code_repos) merge with the configured entries (`code_repos_json` and the scalar entry); a configured entry for a namespace a member added from the page is skipped. Off = the operator's JSON is the only source.

code_self_service_max_repos.description: Active self-service entries per org (branches count); past it the add refuses with a message.

code_setting_control.description: The setting code.setting_facts must find before it claims `not_a_setting` for any other name; empty = it never claims it.

code_shell_chunk_target_chars.description: Leftover coalescing target in chars for shell files.

code_shell_islands.description: A shell test's SQL strings (`$CLICKHOUSE_CLIENT -q`, heredocs, `echo |`) become `statement` symbols with facets; leftover chunks coalesce up to `code_shell_chunk_target_chars`, never across a function. Needs a `--paths-file` backfill.

code_sql_chunk_target_chars.description: Statement packing target (chars); a larger single statement splits at lines at `code_chunk_max_chars`.

code_sql_column_lineage.description: Column-level SQL lineage: `<table>.<column>` symbols, `column_read` / `column_write` facets and statement → column edges, for `.sql` and Python SQL islands. Off = table-level lineage. Needs a `--paths-file` backfill.

code_sql_statement_records.description: SQL tests as statement records: one `statement` symbol per record, chunks packed by whole statements, facet rows in loom.code_test_facets. Off = line-window chunks for `.sql`. Existing namespaces need `loom code backfill --paths-file` (outside the extractor stamp).

code_stale_after_commits.description: as_of.stale is true when the fast tier is more than this many first-parent commits behind the fetched branch tip (60 s cache).

code_status_building_counts_ttl_s.description: Seconds an entry's chunk counts are cached while it is still building: they move then without a watermark moving.

code_status_ledger_passes_ttl_s.description: Seconds code.repos keeps the worker-ledger answer every repository's status shares.

code_status_recent_commits_ttl_s.description: Seconds a repository's recent-commits listing for code.repos is cached.

code_status_steady_counts_ttl_s.description: Seconds an indexed entry's chunk counts are cached once it is no longer building.

code_status_symbol_stats_ttl_s.description: Seconds an entry's symbol statistics are cached for its status.

code_status_ttl_s.description: Seconds one (org, namespace)'s index status serves every caller before it is computed again.

code_summary_churn_days.description: Days of merged PRs the summary cards' churn order counts: a bounded card pass considers files by merged-PR count per path over these days (source tree), then by include-graph rank.

code_summary_churn_exclude.description: CSV of path prefixes the summary cards' churn order never proposes, at any depth (vendored trees).

code_summary_churn_prefixes.description: CSV path prefixes the summary cards' churn order may propose; empty = any.

code_summary_concurrency.description: Cards in flight per pass; 1 = sequential.

code_summary_max_scopes_per_pass.description: Cards written per pass across every repository, shared out evenly (a share one repository does not use rolls to the next).

code_summary_upgrade_from_models.description: CSV of summary models whose cards are rewritten when code_summary_model differs, even for an unchanged file. Empty = an unchanged file keeps its card.

code_symbol_uses_hub_fan_in.description: Fan-in at or above which the `uses` block says `skipped: hub` instead of listing sites. 0 = never.

code_test_gate_run_templates.description: code.test_gate run recipes (LOOM_CODE_TEST_GATE_RUN_TEMPLATES): JSON list of {"pattern": <regex over the repo-relative test path>, "run": <template>}, tried before the built-ins. Templates may use {path} {dir} {stem} {name} {parent}. A path no recipe matches is reported run_unknown, never guessed.

code_tier_failing_error_lag_commits.description: A `code_tier_failing` health problem is an error when the failing tier is also this many commits behind the fetched tip; the fetch tier, whose lag is unknown, stays a warn.

code_tier_failing_warn_hours.description: A code-index tier failing for this many hours is a `code_tier_failing` health problem (warn), however few passes ran in that time.

code_tier_failing_warn_passes.description: A code-index tier failing this many passes in a row is a `code_tier_failing` health problem (warn); fewer is a transient failure the next pass retries.

code_unit_risk_max_age_s.description: Age (seconds) past which a risk row is stale and annotated live; must exceed the weekly pass interval.

code_vector_tables.description: JSON {label: {"table": "loom.x", "dim": 256}}: where a label's chunk rows live (the coded vector column is fixed-width). Absent label = loom.code_chunks. Inserts and the vector leg route by it.

conflict_resolver_model.description: The conflict resolver's judge (memory_conflict_resolver_enabled). Its confidence thresholds were set on this model; a cheaper one is only safe for clears.

conflict_threshold.description: memory.set flags a write `conflicted` when an active peer in the same (org, namespace, memory_type) sits at cosine ≥ this. Tuned for text-embedding-3-*; 1.0 disables. Per-namespace override: loom.namespaces.conflict_threshold.

consolidation_merge_concurrency.description: Clusters merged concurrently by memory.consolidate; 1 = sequential.

context_offload_max_bytes.description: context.offload: largest single parked tool result, in bytes.

conversation_search_excerpt_chars.description: Characters of a turn a conversation search hit or a saved-message listing shows; it changes no stored row. At most 2048, the most an embedding row stores (EMBEDDED_EXCERPT_CHARS), so the vector path can always fill it. A saved-message listing reads this many characters and a fixed margin past them, and checks them all for a high shape before it cuts the excerpt.

conversation_search_min_similarity.description: conversation.search cosine floor; without it the top_k nearest threads return however far. Stricter than memory recall: chat excerpts are noisy.

conversation_titler_enabled.description: LLM-title untitled threads in namespaces with conversation_logging_enabled (the Record conversations switch on the dashboard's Conversations page is the off-switch). Skipped with the fake LLM.

conversation_titler_max_threads_per_pass.description: Threads one pass titles at most.

conversation_titler_min_turns.description: Turns a thread needs before it is titled.

conversation_titler_window_hours.description: Only threads with a turn in the last this-many hours are titled.

cors_origins.description: Comma-separated origin list. "*" allows all (acceptable when auth_required=True). Empty disables CORS entirely.

dashboard_redirect_url.description: When set, a dashboard page load redirects (302) here instead of serving the SPA (Loom behind an aggregator). Deployment-specific; never hardcode.

default_daily_cost_cap_usd.description: Daily LLM spend cap per namespace, USD: extraction workers skip a namespace whose rolling 24 h cost reached it. Overridden per namespace by loom.namespaces.daily_cost_cap_usd; 0.0 disables on both tiers.

default_namespace.description: The one namespace auth-off mode serves (SPA identity, dashboard bootstrap, MCP/SDK caller defaults). Ignored when auth is required; `personal-*` is reserved and rejected.

delete_version_check_batch_size.description: Delete-version checks one delete_version_check pass runs.

delete_version_check_enabled.description: Run the delete_version_check worker, which finishes the memory.delete_version checks a 503 left owed (False: only a retry of the delete finishes them).

delete_version_check_grace_seconds.description: Seconds a delete-version check is left to the delete that owes it before a pass runs it.

delete_version_check_idle_interval_secon.description: Seconds between delete_version_check passes that found none.

delete_version_check_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between delete_version_check passes while checks are owed.

deployment.description: True marks this process as the deployment itself: its compose files set LOOM_DEPLOYMENT=1, and every other process sets LOOM_INSTANCE_LABEL instead (e.g. `iso:<worktree>:<port>`, `ci:integration`). A process with neither refuses to start, so every ledger row is attributable.

document_blob_gc_enabled.description: The sweep that deletes originals no live document points at: those of deleted and re-uploaded documents, and of documents that retention (retention_documents_days, a namespace's retention_days; the ClickHouse authority only) aged out. Their bucket objects go with them; a walk of the bucket deletes any object left.

document_blob_gc_object_pages.description: Pages of 1,000 bucket keys the sweep's walk reads a pass, from where the last stopped: one walk takes a pass per this many thousand keys.

document_blob_min_age_seconds.description: Seconds an original must have gone unwritten before the sweep may remove it. A write stores its original before the document row that names it, so a younger original may belong to a write still in flight. Erasure ignores it and deletes every original of its scope. With a bucket, the settings refuse one under a minimum: a write's upload budget plus its row insert's retries (906 s at the defaults; a much larger value leaves room for what the minimum does not count), or an unbounded write timeout, read timeout or pool wait.

document_extractor_max_artifact_bytes.description: Bytes of an extractor's response the server reads; a larger artifact is refused.

document_extractor_timeout_s.description: Seconds one call to an extractor may take as a whole: reading its capabilities, or sending the original and reading its artifact.

document_object_store.description: Where a new original's bytes go: `clickhouse` (the row's `data`) or `s3` (an object in document_s3_bucket); an original is read from where its row says.

document_s3_bucket.description: The S3-compatible bucket originals are written to, read from and erased from; required with document_object_store=s3 and while any object is left under the prefix.

document_s3_connect_timeout_s.description: Seconds a request to document_s3_bucket may take to connect; past it the request fails as a store error (503).

document_s3_endpoint_url.description: Endpoint of an S3-compatible store; empty is AWS S3 for document_s3_region.

document_s3_prefix.description: Key prefix inside document_s3_bucket; each object is `<prefix>/<org>/<namespace>/<sha256>/<write id>`.

document_s3_read_timeout_s.description: Seconds a request to document_s3_bucket may take to answer (a streamed download, per chunk); past it the request fails as a store error (503).

document_s3_region.description: Region of document_s3_bucket; empty takes the credential chain's region.

duplicate_threshold.description: Cosine ≥ this with a canonical-form mismatch marks a write 'duplicate' with a duplicate_of pointer instead of 'conflicted'. Per-namespace override: loom.namespaces.duplicate_threshold.

embedding_base_url.description: API root for an explicitly selected OpenAI-compatible embedding service, e.g. https://provider.example/v1. Empty is invalid for compatible providers.

embedding_cache_shared.description: Shared query-embedding cache in loom.embedding_cache behind the per-process LRU, rows keyed (model, sha1(org, model, version salt, normalised text)); a call outside a request skips both tiers. Only single-text (query) embeds up to `embedding_cache_shared_max_chars` (0 = no cap) use it. Off = process cache only.

embedding_cache_shared_max_chars.description: Longest query text, characters, that uses the shared cache; 0 = no cap.

embedding_cache_size.description: Entries the per-process query-embedding LRU holds; 0 = cache nothing.

embedding_cache_ttl_s.description: Seconds one per-process LRU entry lives.

embedding_dim.description: Vector width the embedder is asked for and the schema is sized from; the width probed from the embedder at boot wins when they differ. Change it together with `embedding_model`. Unset with a `local:*` model, it is that model's own width: leave it unset for a local model.

embedding_model.description: Embeddings for memories, queries and code chunks. fake-ngram-3072 needs no network or key; production uses text-embedding-3-* (OPENAI_API_KEY). Change it together with `embedding_dim`; a new embedding space needs a full re-embed.

embedding_provider.description: "" = infer from `embedding_model` (fake-ngram-* → fake, text-embedding-* → openai, gemini* → gemini, local/local:* → local CPU embedder); or pin "openai", "gemini", "local", "fake". Switching providers changes the embedding space: a full re-embed is required.

embedding_retry_attempts.description: Attempts an embedding call makes on a retryable failure.

embedding_retry_max_wait_s.description: Longest backoff, in seconds, between two attempts of an embedding call.

embedding_send_dimensions.description: Send the optional dimensions request parameter to a compatible endpoint. False uses its native output width; responses must still match embedding_dim.

embedding_worker_enabled.description: Recovery worker: retries failed embeds and reconciles orphan scope='shared' rows (the write path embeds inline).

embedding_worker_idle_interval_seconds.description: Sleep after an idle embedding recovery pass (nothing to embed); `embedding_worker_interval_seconds` resumes once a pass writes a row.

embedding_worker_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between recovery worker passes while there is work.

embedding_worker_orphan_full_scan_second.description: Seconds between orphan reconciliation's full memory × embedding anti-joins; other passes check only memories of the last `embedding_worker_orphan_recent_seconds`. 0 = full join every pass.

embedding_worker_orphan_recent_seconds.description: Age window, seconds, of the memories a non-full orphan pass checks.

entity_communities_enabled.description: Label-propagation communities over the entity co-occurrence graph, per namespace, into loom.entity_communities (read by namespace.taxonomy and graph-mode expansion). A CPU pass over every namespace's edges.

entity_communities_giant_share.description: When one community holds more than this share of a namespace's entities, double `entity_communities_hub_drop_fraction` and re-partition, up to `entity_communities_hub_drop_max_fraction` (a code corpus parted at 0.016, 2.9%). 0 = fixed fraction.

entity_communities_hub_drop_fraction.description: Leave the top fraction of entities by degree out of the partition, so generic tokens cannot fuse the graph into one community. A graph under 500 entities drops none. 0 = keep every entity.

entity_communities_hub_drop_max_fraction.description: Largest `entity_communities_hub_drop_fraction` the re-partition doubles up to (four doublings from its default); a graph still fused here is written as is and counted in the pass outcome.

entity_communities_max_edges.description: Entity pairs read per namespace, strongest first; past it the rest are dropped and the namespace is reported truncated.

entity_communities_min_co_occur.description: Co-occurrence count an entity pair needs to count as an edge.

entity_communities_walked_days.description: A pass covers the namespaces with consolidation_enabled plus those whose graph was walked (facts.traverse / related / path, namespace.taxonomy) within this many days; 0 = the opted-in set only.

entity_extract_backlog_per_namespace.description: Backlog keys per namespace in one refill, oldest first, round-robin across namespaces so one cannot starve the rest. 0 = org-wide newest first.

entity_extract_enabled.description: Async LLM entity tagging of memory rows (fills `entities` for search's entity match); off the memory.set hot path.

entity_extract_full_scan_keys.description: Keys the full scan queues for the passes in between (refilled early when the queue runs dry).

entity_extract_full_scan_seconds.description: Seconds between entity extraction's full candidate scans (without the value column); other passes scan only `entity_extract_recent_seconds`. 0 = full scan every pass.

entity_extract_idle_interval_seconds.description: Sleep after an entity extraction pass that found no unentitied row.

entity_extract_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between entity extraction passes that found work.

entity_extract_recent_seconds.description: Window, seconds, of recent memories each pass scans for untagged rows.

entity_heal_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between the entity extractor's mirror divergence heal, a FINAL-to-FINAL join of loom.memory and loom.memory_embeddings (343 GB/day if run every pass). Divergence arrives a few rows a day.

erasure_event_drain_timeout_s.description: Seconds erasure waits for this replica's buffered events before deleting them; a timeout leaves the saga retryable. Must be positive and finite.

erasure_export_conversation_max_bytes.description: Bytes of conversation text after which `erasure.export` stops its `conversations` section, marked `truncated`; a page holds up to this plus the turn that crosses it.

erasure_ledger_days.description: Days `loom.erasure_ledger` keeps each erasure under the Postgres authority: the oldest backup's age plus the longest an erasure runs (at most 89, as ClickHouse's ledger reads).

erasure_mutation_wait_s.description: Seconds one erasure step waits for its mutation (submitted with mutations_sync=0, polled in system.mutations); past it the saga fails naming the mutation.

erasure_reclaim_enabled.description: Physically remove purged rows: a purge of a wide table only masks its rows (lightweight DELETE), and large settled parts rarely merge, so the bytes stay. The erasure reclaim worker gives the purge table with the most dead bytes one `APPLY DELETED MASK` per pass. False = the masked rows wait for merges.

erasure_reclaim_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between passes of the erasure reclaim worker.
