erasure_reclaim_min_dead_bytes.description: Least bytes the deleted rows must hold before the erasure reclaim compacts a table (default 1 GiB).

erasure_reclaim_min_dead_fraction.description: A table is reclaimed once this share of its rows on disk are purged rows.

erasure_recovery_enabled.description: Replay erasure sagas stuck `in_progress` past a heartbeat from `steps_completed`.

erasure_recovery_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between passes of the erasure recovery worker.

events_stream_flush_batch.description: Queued telemetry rows that trigger a flush before the interval elapses.

events_stream_flush_interval_s.description: Flush cadence of the loom.events queue (budget violations); also the visibility delay of those rows and the loss window on a process crash.

external_erasure_timeout_s.description: Per-request seconds for external trace/chat backend lookups and deletes during erasure.

extraction_defer_agents.description: Agents whose set_from_messages runs deferred without the flag: comma-separated agent names, "*" = every service-account caller, "" = nobody. A call that sets `record_schema` is never deferred by this list (it reads `written` back), and an explicit defer=false still wins.

extraction_policy_max_namespaces.description: Most namespaces of one org that may hold their own extraction policy; `extraction_policy.set` with scope `namespace` refuses one more.

extraction_queue_enabled.description: Deferred set_from_messages replay. On by default: `defer` is opt-in per call, and an empty queue costs one SELECT per interval.

extraction_queue_lease_seconds.description: Seconds a claimed batch stays leased to one worker before another may claim it; at least a minute. Set it above the longest pass (`extraction_queue_max_batches_per_pass` times one replay), or an overlapping worker may claim a batch still waiting in the pass.

extraction_queue_max_attempts.description: Attempts before a failing batch stops returning to `pending` and is marked failed; each failure waits 15 s, 1, 5, then 30 minutes before the next. A model provider or gateway that cannot be reached, or a held call, spends none.

extraction_queue_max_batches_per_pass.description: Most queued batches one pass claims.

extraction_queue_namespace_concurrency.description: Namespaces replayed concurrently per pass; batches inside one namespace stay serial in session-date order. At least 1: none would hang the pass.

facts_traverse_hub_share.description: Relative hub rule: hold a reached node when the edge that reached it is at most this share of the node's degree (via_co_occur / degree). Scale-free. 0 = off; a request's `hub_share` overrides it.

facts_traverse_rank_by.description: What facts.traverse's per-hop trim ranks by: `co_occur` (most co-mentioned pairs), `specificity` (via_co_occur / degree; request option only, it fills hop 1 with singletons) or `cosine` (via_co_occur / sqrt(degree)).

git_history.description: Where git-history reads (blame, citation commit checks, PR history, commit coverage) come from. local = this host's mirrors; none = an edge host with no mirrors: those reads answer without history.

grant_cache_ttl_seconds.description: Seconds a subject's grant rows are cached for the namespace gate, which caps a token's claim at the grant it holds there. The backstop: a grant change reaches other processes through the per-org grant watermark (acl_watermark_poll_seconds), and this bounds one whose watermark row was never written. It also bounds how long a SCIM deactivation of an email, or a bot disable, takes to stop a trusted caller acting for it on another process, and how long a bot created there takes to be acted for.

hsts_max_age_seconds.description: Strict-Transport-Security max-age, seconds; browsers ignore it over plain HTTP. 0 sends no header.

http_client_connect_timeout_s.description: Seconds the shared outbound HTTP clients wait to open a connection.

http_client_max_connections.description: Connections each shared outbound HTTP client keeps open at most, so one misbehaving downstream cannot exhaust the process's sockets.

http_client_max_keepalive_connections.description: Idle connections each shared outbound HTTP client keeps for reuse.

http_client_timeout_s.description: Seconds the shared outbound HTTP clients (server/clients/_http.py: model and embedding APIs, GitHub, issuer discovery, provider checks) wait on a call that sets no timeout of its own. Read when a process builds the clients.

identity_provider.description: How callers authenticate: "single-user" (no auth, one anonymous identity), "trust-network" (self-signup, first claim wins) or "gateway" (an upstream proxy mints short-lived Loom JWTs with the shared HS256 secret; Loom only validates). Empty = inferred from auth_required and self_signup at boot.

identity_provider_timeout_s.description: Seconds one call to an identity provider may take: OIDC discovery, the token and revocation endpoints, its signing keys, a machine issuer's discovery, and an end-user issuer's JWKS fetch.

inference_customer_format.description: How the customer header names an org, as the gateway knows it: `{org}` is the org id, around it letters, digits and . _ ~ : @ - only ("{org}" = the id as is).

inference_customer_header.description: Header naming the customer (the org) on every model call, for a gateway that meters by it; set, a call naming no customer is refused (server/llm/customer.py).

inference_customer_required.description: True (a cell serving several customers): refuse to start without inference_customer_header, so no model call goes out unattributed.

inference_feature_header.description: Header naming the feature that made the call (hyde, memory.search, worker.embedding, ...), with inference_customer_header only; "" sends none.

inference_feature_map_json.description: JSON object from Loom's feature names (hyde, memory.search, worker.embedding, ...) to the gateway's (letters, digits, . _ ~ : @ -); "*" for any other; "" = Loom's.

inference_gateway_hosts.description: Comma-separated hostnames (exact, any case) of the gateway; required, and the only hosts sent to, while the gateway is required.

inference_gateway_required.description: True: model calls and memory content go only to inference_gateway_hosts; on whenever a workload token is sent (inference_token_url, or the bearer mode).

inference_identity_headers_json.description: JSON object {header: template} every model call carries, naming whom it is for: {org} {namespace} {subject} {user_id}, {agent} (of a workload trust's agent token), {tenant} (that trust's inference_tenant_claim) and {email} (a person's). A header whose template renders empty is not sent, and those naming {agent} or {tenant} go together or not at all; set, a call naming no org is refused. "" sends none (server/llm/identity.py).

inference_identity_refusals_json.description: JSON object of the gateway answers that hold one identity, not the provider: {"refused": [...], "wait": [...]}, each entry {"status": <int>} and at least one of the error body's exact "code", "type" or "message". A refused identity's job work waits inference_refusal_cooldown_seconds, a waiting one the answer's Retry-After. The default: an agent over its budget (by code, and by type and message where the Anthropic-shaped answer carries no code), denied, or named incompletely or malformed; too many of its requests in progress waits. Never list an answer the gateway also gives for its own failure (a credential it cannot fetch, no default agent): health would stop seeing it. Read only with identity headers set (server/llm/gateway.py).

inference_refusal_cooldown_seconds.description: Seconds a background job leaves the work of an identity the gateway refused (an answer listed under "refused") before it calls for it again; 0 calls again at once.

inference_system_customer.description: The customer named on calls made for the deployment itself (startup probe, the recalibration worker's fixed pairs, provider checks), which belong to no org.

inference_tenant_claim.description: The workload trust claim {tenant} names: the value the trust requires of it, exactly.

inference_token_audience.description: With inference_token_url and no workload token: the audience of the identity token Loom signs (issuer <https public_base_url>/v1, newest RS256 key); never jwt_audience.

inference_token_exchange_timeout_s.description: Seconds one token exchange with the inference gateway may take.

inference_token_scope.description: The scope sent with the inference gateway token exchange; "" sends none.

inference_token_url.description: Model calls with no provider key: exchange an identity token (RFC 8693) at this token endpoint of the gateway, and send the answer as the bearer (server/llm/gateway.py). The gateway must trust the token's issuer. "" = the provider keys.

inference_workload_token_file.description: The workload's OIDC token, as a file its platform rotates (a projected service-account token on Kubernetes). With inference_token_url, this or inference_token_audience.

inference_workload_token_mode.description: How inference_workload_token_file reaches the gateway: "exchange" (RFC 8693, at inference_token_url) or "bearer" (the file itself, read again at most every minute and after a 401; requires the gateway).

insights_agents_connected_ttl_s.description: Seconds one agents.connected answer per (org, namespace, window, caller) is reused: the sidebar badge asks every 30 s per tab and the answer is a 24 h scan of agent_events.

instance_heartbeat_seconds.description: Seconds between this process's loom.instances heartbeats, each of which also compares it with the deployment's published configuration. A row not renewed for three intervals is not live.

jwt_audience.description: The `aud` claim stamped on minted tokens and required on every verified token.

jwt_end_user_issuers_json.description: The services that sign a short-lived token per end user (a chat app in front of Loom): JSON (or base64 JSON) {issuer: {"orgs": [...], "jwks_url": "https://…", "keys": {kid: RS256 public PEM}}}. `orgs` lists the orgs its tokens may name (exact names, or `prefix*`); its keys come from `jwks_url` (fetched every `jwt_end_user_jwks_refresh_seconds`) and/or `keys`. A key here verifies only its own issuer's tokens, and only as an end user (`sub: user:<id>`, one listed `org`, an optional `agent: agent:<id>`), never any other token. Empty: no end-user tokens. A non-loopback bind refuses an inline RSA key under 2048 bits (a key fetched from `jwks_url` is not checked).

jwt_end_user_jwks_refresh_seconds.description: Seconds between fetches of each end-user issuer's `jwks_url`; a key it rotates in is honoured from the next fetch.

jwt_end_user_max_ttl_seconds.description: The longest an end-user token may live, from its `iat` to its `exp`.

jwt_issuer.description: The `iss` Loom stamps on every token it mints; a verified token carries it or one of `jwt_trusted_issuers`.

jwt_keyring_refresh_seconds.description: Seconds between re-reads of loom.signing_keys in every process (at least 1); `loom signing-key rotate` waits out two of the slowest process's.

jwt_leeway_seconds.description: Clock-skew tolerance on iat/exp, seconds; small enough to give replay no useful post-exp window.

jwt_revocation_cache_ttl_seconds.description: Seconds the `loom.revoked_tokens` snapshot is cached; verify checks both jti and sub against it, so a revocation takes effect on other processes within this TTL (at once on the one that wrote it).

jwt_revocation_max_stale_seconds.description: Oldest revocation snapshot a process still trusts, seconds. Past it (refreshes keep failing) every bearer is refused with a retryable 503. A subject's cached grants are trusted as long when a re-read fails.

jwt_trusted_issuers.description: Extra accepted `iss` values, for a gateway minting Loom-shaped JWTs with a key in `jwt_public_keys_json`. Loom's own tokens (iss = jwt_issuer) pass.

keeper_sweep_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between passes of the always-on sweep that deletes the KeeperMap keys (leases, claims, graph slots) a stopped process left behind.

knowledge_bm25_corpus_ttl_s.description: Seconds the BM25 corpus statistics of a knowledge namespace are cached.

knowledge_chunk_size.description: Sliding-window chunking on knowledge.add/upsert, in characters. chunk_size 0 = one chunk per doc (hurts long-form retrieval). Smaller chunks mean more embed calls; 1500/1230 stays well under the text-embedding-3 context.

knowledge_chunk_stride.description: Characters between chunk starts: below chunk_size the chunks overlap; above it the step is chunk_size, so no text falls between chunks.

knowledge_ingest_enabled.description: The worker that runs ingestion jobs: extract, chunk, embed, publish.

knowledge_ingest_idle_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between passes when the last one found nothing to do.

knowledge_ingest_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between ingestion passes while jobs wait; 0 takes the next job as soon as one ends, so the queue drains at the speed of its jobs.

knowledge_ingest_max_attempts.description: Attempts a job gets after a transient failure (a provider or store outage) before it fails for good.

knowledge_ingest_max_chunks.description: Most chunks one source may publish; a larger extraction fails with `too_large` rather than flood the embedder.

knowledge_ingest_max_pass_seconds.description: Seconds one pass, which runs one job, may take before it is cancelled: the extractor's timeout plus embedding the largest source. A job cut off runs again from its start and counts toward its attempts.

knowledge_noise_filter.description: True: noise sections rank below the knowledge hits close to the query and stay out of context.pack and memory.stack. False: they are served like any section.

knowledge_orphan_chunk_min_age_seconds.description: Seconds a no-row source's chunks must have aged before a delete retires them (a first write's are younger); never less than an ingest pass plus 5 minutes of clock skew.

knowledge_repo_docs_list_ttl_s.description: Seconds a repository's document list is cached for the docs section of a brief.

knowledge_repo_docs_timeout_s.description: Seconds the repository-docs read for a brief may take.

knowledge_search_fanout_kinds.description: Namespace kinds an all_mine knowledge.search spans (comma list over loom.namespaces.kind): the memory fan-out's, and the caller's collections.

knowledge_search_max_namespaces.description: Namespaces an all_mine knowledge.search reads besides the addressed one, at most; the rest come back in `namespaces_skipped`. Each search leg is one statement over all of them (measured 110 ms at 10,000 collections).

knowledge_search_rerank_default.description: Reranker knowledge.search uses when the request names none (same values as the per-request `rerank`: a builtin or a name in LOOM_RERANK_ENDPOINTS_JSON; rerank="none" turns it off for a call). Empty = no default rerank.

knowledge_search_rerank_excerpt_chars.description: Characters of each hit a reranker reads: its context (title, description, breadcrumb; at most half), then the chunk text. builtin:cohere reads at most 1024.

knowledge_search_rerank_timeout_s.description: Seconds a knowledge.search waits on its reranker before it keeps the fused order.

knowledge_search_rerank_top.description: How many fused hits a rerank reads (the legs fetch at least this many).

knowledge_source_probe_timeout_s.description: Seconds a document source's probe (add, check, rotate) may take in all; past it add and rotate answer SOURCE_UNREACHABLE and check answers reachable: false.

knowledge_source_sync_cap_share.description: The share of a namespace's daily LLM cost cap the sync may spend mining changed documents for decisions, counted over its own calls; the rest stays for requests.

knowledge_source_sync_documents_per_pass.description: Documents one pass fetches, writes, retires or mines for decisions across all sources; the rest wait for the next pass.

knowledge_source_sync_enabled.description: The knowledge_source_sync worker: pulls each registered document source's changed files into its repository's documents. Off by default: it needs each source's credential, spends embedding calls on every changed document and model calls mining it for decisions.

knowledge_source_sync_full_interval_seco.description: Seconds after which a source's next pass lists every file, not only those changed since the last one: what finds a file trashed or moved out of a folder.

knowledge_source_sync_idle_interval_seco.description: Seconds between passes that found no source to sync; one idle sleep plus one pass stays under three intervals, so the worker never reads as stalled.

knowledge_source_sync_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between sync passes while there are sources.

knowledge_source_sync_max_file_bytes.description: Bytes of one file a sync downloads or exports; a larger file is not ingested.

knowledge_source_sync_max_pass_seconds.description: Seconds one sync pass may run before it is cancelled; it stops starting sources at three quarters of it. At least 180: 90 for the sync, then 60 of read time for one document's extraction and 30 for its writes before the deadline.

knowledge_sources_max_per_namespace.description: Active document sources (knowledge.source.add) one repository namespace may register; an add past it is refused with SOURCE_QUOTA.

knowledge_upload_max_bytes.description: Largest file POST /v1/knowledge.upload accepts, in bytes; a larger body is refused with 413 before any of it is stored.

knowledge_upload_ttl_seconds.description: Seconds an upload stays ingestible; the originals sweep keeps its bytes until then, and knowledge.ingest refuses it after.

langfuse_capture_io_level.description: How much LLM prompt and completion text is recorded, by what the prompt holds: "off" records none (the default; consent is given, not withdrawn); "query" only the legs whose prompt is the user's own search text (hyde, query_rewrite, enrichment, …); "all" also the legs carrying retrieved memories or conversation turns (inline_rerank, iterative_judge, extract, session_summary, …). A namespace's `capture_generation_io` overrides it (false ⇒ off, true ⇒ all, NULL ⇒ this). It also gates loom.search_trace_log.query. Token counts, cost, latency and quality scores are never gated.

langfuse_circuit_cooldown_s.description: Seconds the open breaker waits before a trial call (floor 1).

langfuse_circuit_failure_threshold.description: Score-POST circuit breaker: consecutive failures that open it.

langfuse_generation_io_max_chars.description: Per-field cap on recorded prompt/completion text; truncation adds an explicit marker.

langfuse_sample_rate.description: Fraction of TRACES forwarded, sampled by trace id so a trace arrives whole. Span volume is dominated by worker embeddings; turn down in production.

langfuse_span_denylist.description: Span-name prefixes never forwarded: high-volume infrastructure spans with no LLM work (they belong in ClickStack).

langfuse_timeout_s.description: Seconds one Langfuse API call may take: posting a score, and the traces and scores the prompt evaluation reads.

langfuse_url.description: Langfuse: with both set, OTel spans are forwarded to Langfuse's OTLP endpoint as a second span processor beside the ClickHouse exporter, retrieval scores are posted, and the erasure saga makes real HTTP DELETE calls (empty = log intent only). The token is `pk-lf-…:sk-lf-…`.

latency_budget_multiplier.description: Scales every op's p99 budget (OP_BUDGETS_P99_MS in server/settings/catalog.py, tuned for local CH) at the comparison site; set e.g. 20.0 on Cloud so SLO alerts don't fire on baseline RTT.

latency_budget_overrides.description: JSON map {op: ms | "<n>x"} over the op budgets table (OP_BUDGETS_P99_MS in server/settings/catalog.py): an integer replaces that op's budget, "3x" multiplies it. Checked after the per-consumer overrides and `admin/budget.set`; a value that is neither ms nor "<n>x" stops startup, an op this build lacks is logged and ignored. '' = the table as declared.

latency_budget_overrides_by_consumer.description: JSON map {consumer: {op | "*": ms | "<n>x"}}: an integer is a budget in ms, "3x" multiplies the op's declared budget. Checked after runtime `admin/budget.set` overrides, before per-op ones; malformed = logged once and ignored. '' = none.

llm_anthropic_effort.description: Thinking effort sent to Claude models as `output_config.effort`: "low" | "medium" | "high"; "" = send none (the model's own default). A model that does not take it refuses it once and is not sent it again.

llm_fallback_model.description: Model to answer with when a client's provider is still unavailable after its retries (429 / 5xx / transport / timeout) or rejected the request (400 / 413 / 422). Counted in `loom.llm.fallback`. 401 / 403 / 404 are configuration and never fall back. "" = fail the op.

llm_hidden_reasoning_reserve_max.description: Most output tokens a call adds over the caller's cap for a model's hidden reasoning. The reserve per model is learned from the reasoning tokens its replies report (twice the most it has spent) and capped here.

llm_max_tokens_overrides.description: JSON {call: tokens} over LLM_MAX_TOKENS (in server/settings/catalog.py): the most tokens one kind of LLM call may write, keyed by its `llm_stage`. A count below 1 is refused; a call this build lacks is logged and ignored. '' = the table as declared.

llm_model.description: The deployment's LLM: memory extraction, rerank and every job whose own model setting (the other *_model settings) is left "". Empty takes the resolved provider's default model (gpt-6-luna / claude-haiku-4-5 / fake-echo-1).

llm_openai_reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort sent to OpenAI models. "" = the lowest the model accepts (learned from its refusals, see server/llm/traits.py); set to pin one value for every call.

llm_policy_by_traffic_class.description: JSON {class: {"llm_cache": bool, "strong": bool, "mid": bool}}: `llm_cache` overrides the class's cache default (a per-request pin wins); `strong`/`mid` false bars the cascade from that tier. Unlisted = every tier eligible.

llm_provider.description: "openai" | "anthropic" | "fake"; "" = infer from LOOM_LLM_MODEL's name (gpt*/o1*/o3*/o4*/chatgpt* → openai, claude* → anthropic, fake* → fake), else from the key present (OPENAI_API_KEY, then ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), else fake. Resolved once at load; an explicit value is never overridden. Run `make bench-quick` before making anthropic a default.

llm_request_timeout_s.description: Seconds an LLM call waits for its reply before the client retries. Generous on purpose: it only catches a hung connection, so a slow model or a long output never hits it. Calls that must be fast set their own, shorter deadline (HyDE, search budgets).

llm_rerank_skip_above.description: Skip the rerank when the vector top hit's cosine is ≥ this (strong matches rank reliably; the rerank costs ~500 ms). Fallback when the adaptive gate has no probe.

llm_response_cache_table.description: The table the LLM response cache reads and writes; an isolated server whose boot migrations are off points this at its own scratch mirror.

llm_retry_attempts.description: Attempts an LLM call makes on a retryable failure (a 429, a 5xx, a dropped connection) before the fallback model takes over.

llm_retry_max_wait_s.description: Longest backoff, in seconds, between two attempts of an LLM call.

local_embedding_model_dir.description: Where `local` models live (relative: under the working directory), one directory per alias and revision; a missing file is fetched there. The image sets it by env.

log_level.description: Root log level. (Bind host/port are flags of `loom serve`, not settings.)

max_request_bytes.description: Request-body cap, bytes, enforced by ASGI middleware before any parser (413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE); uvicorn has no limit of its own. 0 disables.

mcp_always_load_tools.description: Ops whose tools/list entry carries `_meta: {"anthropic/alwaysLoad": true}`, so a host that defers MCP tools behind tool search lists these up front and an agent calls them on its first turn instead of spending a turn loading them. Comma-separated op names; empty = none.

mcp_auth_mode.description: MCP transport auth mode (the endpoint exposes one tool per wire op, so an anonymous prober could otherwise enumerate every tool): "required"        — every JSON-RPC method requires a bearer. "discovery_only"  — initialize/tools/list/ping open; tools/call needs auth. "open"            — no auth on any method; a non-loopback bind refuses it. Any other value fails at load: a mistyped mode must not boot as some mode.

mcp_code_tools.description: List code.* tools on the MCP surface (core toolset union). Off = code ops are HTTP/SDK-only.

mcp_loom_search_floor_mode.description: Sub-floor rows in loom_search: "drop" serves only what clears the floor; "readmit" (the memory.search default) pads top_k with below-threshold rows the reader is told to ignore; "ids_only" pads with empty bodies.

mcp_loom_search_foreign_margin.description: Extra margin over the precision floor for hits from another namespace.

mcp_loom_search_knowledge_min_similarity.description: loom_search drops knowledge hits below this cosine similarity (the conversation leg's floor, applied to the knowledge leg).

mcp_loom_search_precision_floor.description: Precision floor for loom_search memory hits. Negative = auto (midpoint of the embedder's calibrated noise floor and question→fact p25); 0 disables.

mcp_loom_search_profile_margin.description: Lead a profile section must have over the namespace's runner-up to pass loom_search's soft tier.

mcp_loom_search_profile_min_similarity.description: loom_search's profile leg: sections the words missed pass by cosine against `label\nvalue` at this hard floor. 0 = lexical only.

mcp_loom_search_profile_soft_similarity.description: Cosine floor of loom_search's profile leg for a question about the user only (the soft tier).

mcp_loom_search_tracker_timeout_s.description: Seconds loom_search's tracker leg (similar issues and PRs) may take before the answer goes without it.

mcp_ratelimit_retry_max_wait_s.description: A rate-limited tool call waits out its Retry-After once and re-checks before returning RATE_LIMITED (MCP clients don't retry). This is the longest Retry-After, seconds, that one retry waits out; a longer hint is refused at once, and 0 refuses every limited call at once.

mcp_schema_profile.description: tools/list schema profile: "standard" (curated prose + inputSchema), "full" (+ outputSchema) or "compact" (first paragraph, argument tree). Per request: `?schema_profile=`.

mcp_session_run_idle_seconds.description: Seconds without a tool call after which the mcp_session_run_sweep worker closes an MCP session's implicit run (one per token and `Mcp-Session-Id`, begun on the first run-scoped tool call); with no background workers anywhere, idle runs stay open. At least 60: each web process re-checks its cached run once a minute (mcp_runs.CHECK_INTERVAL_S), so a shorter window would close runs a process still treats as open.

mcp_session_run_sweep_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between passes of the always-on sweep that closes the runs of idle MCP sessions.

mcp_toolset.description: Which tools `tools/list` shows when a connection names no `?toolset=` (a request that names one gets that one instead). Rosters are the frozensets in server/operations/toolsets.py plus loom_search and loom_activate; on every toolset but "assistant" this is visibility only and every op stays callable by name over MCP and /v1/*. "core"      — (default) _MCP_CORE_OPS (+ _MCP_CODE_CORE_OPS when mcp_code_tools is on). "coding"    — _MCP_CODING_OPS + _MCP_CODE_CORE_OPS; the plugin selects it per request with `?toolset=coding`. "tracker", "tasks" — the tracker plane and the task inbox rosters. "atomic"    — CRUD + scratchpad + run ledger (_MCP_ATOMIC_OPS), policy-shaped descriptions. "readonly"  — the "all" listing without the tools whose readOnlyHint is false. "assistant" — MCP_ASSISTANT_OPS only, and only those are callable on a connection that resolves to it. Not a server-wide read-only switch: a request naming another toolset gets it, and the token is the boundary. "all"       — every op except _MCP_HIDDEN_OPS and the experimental ones no curated tier lists (they stay callable by name). An unknown value is "core".

memory_ask_aggregational_window.description: The synthesis window a count question widens to when facet or literal completion adds rows (never narrower than the window it had).

memory_ask_bridge_completion_max.description: Most rows bridge completion adds to the pool.

memory_ask_bridge_completion_per_prefix.description: Most rows bridge completion adds per entity key prefix.

memory_ask_bridge_completion_top_hits.description: Bridge completion: the other attributes of the entities the top hits name (key-prefix siblings) join the pool, so a question that names an entity by one attribute can answer with another. This is the number of top hits whose entities it reads.

memory_ask_bridge_row_hops.description: Hops over the rows — the proper-noun objects of the top hits and their bridged siblings bridge again, twice at most, so a multi-hop question is answered from rows when the triple plane has no path.

memory_ask_code_enrichment.description: Kill-switch for code-plane enrichment: when a query names code-shaped identifiers (a symbol, a File.cpp, a snake_case setting), fuse the bound code index's file:line, symbol and recent PRs into the grounding pool. Additive and fail-open. The opt-in is the code namespace binding (_resolve_code_target): with no per-request override and no memory_ask_code_namespace, enrichment is skipped, hence default on.

memory_ask_code_hop_symbols.description: Symbols the retrieved window names (not only the question) are looked up in the bound code index too, up to this many, one code.symbol definition each, appended after the question's own grounding rows. 0 = off.

memory_ask_code_namespace.description: Code namespace enrichment reads when the request sets none (a per-request override wins). '' = enrichment skipped: with many repos and branches indexed as separate namespaces there is no safe global default. Pair with memory_ask_code_org when the org differs.

memory_ask_code_org.description: Org of memory_ask_code_namespace; "" = code_org, then the ask's own org.

memory_ask_code_search_token_budget.description: Token budget of the code.search read that grounds a code-entity question.

memory_ask_code_staleness.description: Check the code locations a retrieved memory asserts against the live index and flag rotted ones (symbol moved or renamed) so synthesis prefers the current site. Read-time, additive, gated by the code binding; ambiguous symbols are skipped (code_anchor), never false-flagged.

memory_ask_code_symbol_token_budget.description: Token budget of the code.symbol read that grounds a code-entity question in the code plane.

memory_ask_consistency_check.description: After synthesis one judge call (the cheap client when the cascade is on, else the synth client) labels the answer entailed / neutral / contradicted against the memories it cites (consistency, consistency_score, consistency_note). Off: one extra LLM call per synthesized ask.

memory_ask_consistency_mode.description: Where the judge runs. "inline" awaits it and returns the verdict on the wire. "deferred" answers first, leaves the wire fields empty, and writes the verdict as a memory.ask.consistency ledger row (kind='verdict', joined by request_id) plus the contradicted usage event; a precedent is stored only once the verdict is in. A request's consistency field pins either; benches that read the label pin "inline".

memory_ask_context_memories.description: How many top memories the synthesizer sees, independent of the caller's top_k; also sizes the fetch pool and, above 15, the answer-token budget. Raise it only with a strong memory_ask_synth_model, since a weak one dilutes over more items.

memory_ask_count_window.description: Synthesis window for count-shaped questions ("how many X", op=count), whose answer set is scattered across sessions (a missed item sat at rank 18). 0 = no widening.

memory_ask_cue_window_turns_top_k.description: How many user turns dated inside the question's short time window ("a couple of days ago") the not-recorded second reading adds, whatever words they carry.

memory_ask_decisive_chunks.description: For a bug / error / flaky question, read this many verbatim chunks that cite the identifier and carry fix-or-cause vocabulary (root cause, Closes #, backtrace ...) into the pool ahead of the window. 0 = off.

memory_ask_decompose_max_parts.description: Question decomposition (request `decompose`, off when unset): most sub-questions a decomposed question splits into.

memory_ask_decompose_part_top_k.description: Rows retrieved for each decomposed sub-question.

memory_ask_deep_evidence_max_chars.description: Total source-text characters deep evidence may open across all memories of one ask.

memory_ask_deep_evidence_max_chars_per_m.description: Source-text characters deep evidence may open per memory, so a window-linked memory cannot expand into its whole conversation.

memory_ask_deep_evidence_max_memories.description: At most this many memories are opened per ask.

memory_ask_deep_evidence_pool.description: Deep-evidence pass: a selector picks up to memory_ask_deep_evidence_max_memories ranked candidates, their source turns are read (loom.memory_evidence via loom.memory_belief_sources, scoped rows first) and synthesis reruns with the raw turns. Runs on depth="raw" and temporal questions. This field: how many candidates the selector sees (30 = the whole 2x top_k pool).

memory_ask_deep_evidence_select.description: Who picks the memories to open: "llm" = one selection call over the pool; "top" = the top-ranked memories, no LLM call. A request's deep_select overrides.

memory_ask_deep_select_tier.description: Client for the deep selector: "cheap" = the cascade's cheap client when configured, else the routed client; "routed" = the client that synthesizes the answer.

memory_ask_default_answer_chars.description: Default answer length in characters for asks that pass max_answer_chars=0, except breadth questions and structured count/preference/affect answers. 0 = unbounded (synthesis is 88% of ask median latency).

memory_ask_entity_follow_max.description: A chain question ("the citizenship of the CEO of X") follows the first hop's answer entity into one more retrieval per bridge entity; this is the most entities it follows.

memory_ask_entity_follow_top_k.description: Rows retrieved for each followed bridge entity.

memory_ask_exclude_unverified_external.description: memory.ask keeps declared-external, unattested rows out of the synthesis pool (they still surface as hits). Off = they are synthesized like any other row.

memory_ask_facet_completion_max.description: Facet completion: a count question pulls every memory in scope whose key shares the hit keys' attribute facet (user_maya_age -> _age), widening the window to memory_ask_aggregational_window. At most this many rows.

memory_ask_identifier_chase_cap.description: Fact rows the identifier chase (identifiers named by the rows the question's identifier reached) may add across all its hops.

memory_ask_identifier_chase_chunk_cap.description: Verbatim chunks the chase may add, counted apart from memory_ask_identifier_chase_cap. 0 = facts only.

memory_ask_identifier_chase_hops.description: After injection, follow identifier-shaped tokens the injected memories name (a value that is a key, a PR naming a commit) for up to this many more exact-substring reads, adding at most memory_ask_identifier_chase_cap rows. 0 = off. Runs only when the question named an identifier.

memory_ask_identifier_inject_chunks.description: Identifier injection also reads up to this many verbatim chunks (loom.memory_chunks), ranked by cosine to the question; 0 = facts only.

memory_ask_identifier_inject_recent.description: For a disposition / premise / classification question, read this many newest facts and chunks citing the identifier into the pool, and tell the synthesizer the later-dated memory is current when memories on one subject disagree. 0 = off.

memory_ask_identifier_inject_set_facts.description: A set-shaped question about an identifier reads this many fact rows (and twice as many chunks) from the exact fetch instead of eight.

memory_ask_identifier_injection.description: When a query names an identifier (PR/issue number, @handle) that recall missed, inject the memories citing it (exact substring) into the synthesis pool. The lexical leg indexes only alpha tokens >= 3 chars, so bare numbers are otherwise unretrievable. Additive.

memory_ask_knowledge_block_max_chars.description: Characters of the whole knowledge block; the lowest-ranked passages go first.

memory_ask_knowledge_passage_max_chars.description: Characters of one knowledge passage in the answer's context block; longer ones are cut and marked.

memory_ask_knowledge_top_k.description: Passages the knowledge.search leg appends to the synthesis window.

memory_ask_literal_completion_max.description: Count questions: the raw turns naming the question's literal (a place, a number) join the pool, at most this many — a fact the extractor dropped is still a turn.

memory_ask_llm_cache_default.description: Exact-prompt LLM response cache for every memory.ask synthesis-path call, keyed by sha256(org, system, user, max_tokens, response_format) per model in loom.llm_response_cache; a miss writes fire-and-forget. The evidence is in the key, so a changed memory misses. `memory_ask_llm_cache_namespaces` scopes the default; a per-request llm_cache wins (benches measuring synthesis send false).

memory_ask_llm_cache_namespaces.description: Comma-separated fnmatch namespace globs the LLM cache default applies to; '' = all.

memory_ask_mention_window_chunks.description: A question about what was mentioned at a time reads up to this many verbatim chunks whose session date falls in the resolved window (±1 day), cosine-ranked; facts carry the event date, not the mention date. 0 = off.

memory_ask_mid_model.description: memory.ask mid tier. "" = none. With a model set, strong-routed asks whose reason is in memory_ask_synth_mid_routes go mid; an empty, uncited or hedging mid answer escalates to strong once.

memory_ask_order_window_max_days.description: An ordering question with a time cue of up to this many days reads the user's turns from that window with the first synthesis, so a member the extractor left as an aside is listed.

memory_ask_pending_evidence_batches.description: Newest in-flight deferred batches the pending-evidence read scans.

memory_ask_pending_evidence_turns.description: memory.ask pending evidence: the turns of in-flight deferred batches that share words with the question join the synthesis window as raw rows (source="pending"). Most pending turns read into the synthesis window per ask.

memory_ask_pr_grounding.description: For each PR the query or grounding references, inject its authoritative code_pr_history record (author, merged_at, title) as a high-trust grounding fact; the synthesizer prefers it over a memory's older claim (_PR_RECORD_NOTE). Gated by the code binding (_resolve_code_target); additive, fail-open, as-of aware. See _inject_pr_facts. A judged arm shows fewer control regressions with it on than off.

memory_ask_pr_temporal_gate.description: For an as_of query, drop grounding memories that cite a PR opened after the anchor (an under-dated bulk ingest can name a later PR). Open dates come from code_pr_history.opened_at; a no-op without as_of or a bound code index; a PR with an unknown open date is never gated. See _gate_future_prs.

memory_ask_precedents.description: Serve the earlier synthesized answer to the same question and shape, with no LLM call, when the synthesis window is byte-identical (same keys, same content_sha256 per key); otherwise synthesize and store. A per-request precedents field overrides.

memory_ask_precedents_fast_max_age_hours.description: With precedents on, an eligible precedent is served before retrieval when no plane its namespaces read was written since (loom.namespace_write_marks), the blacklist is unchanged and every cited row is live with the same hash; never under the Postgres authority, whose heads ClickHouse's marks can trail. Hours a precedent stays servable on that fast path (a bound on rank drift, not staleness); 0 = no bound.

memory_ask_precedents_max_age_hours.description: Hours a stored precedent stays servable; 0 = no age bound, the evidence alone decides.

memory_ask_precedents_namespaces.description: Comma-separated fnmatch globs the precedent flag applies to; '' = every namespace. Scope it to namespaces whose traffic is real repeats (e.g. "support-*"): on a shared server a paired A/B would answer its second arm from the first.

memory_ask_premise_check.description: When the window holds a pinned or human-verified memory, one judge call asks whether the question presupposes something it contradicts; if so the synthesizer holds the trusted fact and corrects the premise (premise_conflict / premise_note on the wire). One read per ask; an LLM call only with trusted rows in the window.

memory_ask_recency_weight.description: memory.ask only: re-rank the synthesis window by similarity + weight * recency, recency = 1/(1 + age_days/14), so the freshest copy of a fact reaches synthesis. 0.0 = cosine only.

memory_ask_recent_block_max_chars.description: Characters of the whole recent-turns block; the oldest turns go first.

memory_ask_recent_max_turns.description: Conversation turns the recent-turns block carries at most, newest last.

memory_ask_recent_turn_max_chars.description: Characters of one turn in memory.ask's recent-turns block; longer ones are cut and marked.

memory_ask_relevance_gate_min_keep.description: The fewest synthesis rows memory.ask's relevance gate (a cut at the knee of the rows' similarity curve) may leave.

memory_ask_set_full_scan.description: A count or set question reads up to this many rows (window and search pool) instead of the 40-row pool; 0 = off. Such an ask costs about four times a plain one.

memory_ask_set_full_scan_chunk_share.description: When the whole-set scan widens the pool, cap its chunk share so it is mostly fact rows. 0 = uncapped.

memory_ask_set_window.description: Synthesis window for a set question ("what books has she read"), like a count's, since its items sit one per session. 0 = off. MemoryAskInput.set_window overrides.

memory_ask_synth_budget_cheap_ratio.description: Fraction of the namespace's 24 h cost cap at which the cascade routes every ask cheap, with no escalation. 0 = off.

memory_ask_synth_budget_ratio.description: Adaptive synthesis output budget: max(window rule, ratio * evidence tokens), capped at memory_ask_synth_max_tokens_ceiling. The window rule (600 tokens at <= 15 memories, 900 past 15) is the floor; 0 = the window rule alone.

memory_ask_synth_cheap_max_evidence_toke.description: The cheap tier answers only when the synthesis window holds at most this many evidence tokens (chars/4); above it the ask routes strong (cheap losses averaged 5.9k tokens). 0 = off.

memory_ask_synth_max_tokens_ceiling.description: Upper bound on the adaptive budget (a cost and p99 guard, not a target); the provider's own maximum still applies.

memory_ask_synth_mid_routes.description: Which strong-routed reasons go to the mid tier: "uncertain", "off", or a comma list of reason tokens.

memory_ask_synth_model.description: memory.ask synthesis (the strong tier when the cascade is on).

memory_ask_synth_model_cheap.description: memory.ask cheap tier. "" = off: every ask uses memory_ask_synth_model. When set, server/memory/domain/synth_policy.py routes easy asks cheap and hard ones strong; an empty, uncited or hedging cheap answer escalates to strong once. route_tier / route_reason / synth_model on the output record the choice.

memory_ask_synth_route_prior.description: Routing prior from the consistency judge's contradicted rate per route. '' = rule-only router; "measured" = synth_policy.MEASURED_ROUTE_PRIOR; or a JSON object route -> rate. A strong-routed ask whose route rate is <= memory_ask_synth_route_prior_max_cheap goes cheap (reason "<rule>:prior_cheap"); hard stops (identifier, breadth, rich evidence, as_of, ungrounded) never move.

memory_ask_synth_route_prior_max_cheap.description: Route contradicted rate at or below which the routing prior sends a strong-routed ask cheap.

memory_ask_synthesize_route_max_docs.description: A summary-shaped question ("summarize the report") routes to knowledge.synthesize over the documents the knowledge search concentrates on, falling through to the memory path when none concentrates. Documents that route may synthesize over at most.

memory_ask_temporal_deep_select.description: Selector the temporal trigger uses: "llm" (one selection call, about +3 s p50 on temporal asks only) or "top" (no model call). Per-request deep_select overrides.

memory_ask_when_evidence_top_k.description: Dated raw turns the not-recorded second reading recalls.

memory_ask_world_knowledge.description: memory.ask general-knowledge bridging: forbid (default) keeps the synthesizer memory-only; allow lets it combine a memory fact with widely known public facts, marking each bridged sentence, and the output's `grounding` says whether it did. Per-request `world_knowledge` overrides. Agents that must never answer beyond the store keep forbid.

memory_attribute_tagging.description: Tag rows mentioning a protected attribute or common proxy with `attribute:<class>` at write time (gender, religion, health, age, family, income, ethnicity, sexuality, politics). A label, never a gate; the profile fold leaves such rows out.

memory_blacklist_sweep_limit.description: Most memories one blacklist sweep takes from ClickHouse's match (under the Postgres authority it also reads the heads ClickHouse keeps refusing, this many at a time).

memory_bm25_cache_ttl_s.description: Seconds the BM25 corpus statistics (document count, mean length) of a namespace are cached.

memory_bulk_contextualize_allowed.description: memory.bulk_set honours contextualize=true (embed a chunk with its context) only when allowed; `memory_bulk_contextualize_concurrency` bounds the per-entry model calls, `memory_bulk_contextualize_max_entries` caps one call's spend.

memory_bulk_contextualize_concurrency.description: Context model calls one bulk_set runs at once.

memory_bulk_contextualize_max_entries.description: A bulk_set with more pending entries than this is not contextualized at all.

memory_bulk_dedup_scope.description: Bulk-path exact dedup. "session" = a byte-identical value is skipped only under the same key in the same session. "identity" = a live row anywhere in (org, namespace, agent, user_id) with the same content_sha256 is the fact; the entry becomes an `evidence` reinforcement of it, named in `identity_duplicates`.

memory_bulk_follow_max_pairs.description: Supersession pairs one bulk write follows on the triple plane in the request; the rest are recorded for the projection repair to follow. 0 = the repair follows all.

memory_bulk_peer_read.description: How a bulk write reads each fact's conflict and value-update peers: batched = one join per memory_write_candidate_batch facts; per_fact = memory.set's codes-first read per fact, for large namespaces (it may pick another last peer where distances tie).

memory_calibration_namespace_miss_ttl_s.description: Seconds a namespace with no calibration row (or a failed read) is remembered as having none.

memory_calibration_namespace_ttl_s.description: Seconds a namespace's calibration row is cached, so a row written on another replica serves here within it.

memory_capture_structured_answers.description: Capture long / structured / enumerated assistant answers whole (not clipped at EXCERPT_LIMIT) so a positional follow-up resolves: at write time the prompt gains a structured-answer block and assistant-answer facts get a higher content_excerpt ceiling. The value column is untouched; takes effect only on (re-)ingest.

memory_chunks_max_per_call.description: Max ~800-char verbatim chunks one set_from_messages call writes (512 ≈ 400K chars; agent transcripts run ~190K chars a session at the median). Text past the cap is recorded in loom.memory_drops as chunk.split/truncated.

memory_classify_private_hosts.description: Comma-separated hostnames or IP literals, no port, a classify_endpoint may reach on a private address and over http, on any port: list only a host that serves nothing else.

memory_classify_timeout_s.description: Seconds a namespace's classify_endpoint may take to answer a write's classification; past it the write keeps the caller's memory_type.

memory_code_links_batch.description: Memory writes one pass links (at least 1).

memory_code_links_enabled.description: Link memories to the code they name (symbols and files of the repository their `repo:` tag or code namespace names) and keep the links current as the code changes; the namespace's `code_change_policy` decides how reads treat a memory whose code is removed or changed. Off stops linking and rechecks; reads still show the stored states but no longer hide a memory, as nothing keeps them current.

memory_code_links_max_pass_seconds.description: Seconds a code-links pass may run before the supervisor abandons it.

memory_code_links_pending_days.description: Days a code-shaped name that names nothing on trunk yet (unmerged code) is retried before it is dropped.

memory_code_links_revise_per_pass.description: Changed claims one pass re-checks with the LLM under the `revise` policy.

memory_code_links_settle_seconds.description: Seconds the memory code-link pass stays behind the newest queued memory write, so inserts running at the same moment are visible before the cursor passes them (at least 10). A write visible later than this is passed and stays unlinked until a backfill reads it; a longer wait makes that rarer and links every write that much later.

memory_code_links_sweep_interval_s.description: Seconds between the starts of two cycles of the code-links sweep through the link table.

memory_code_plane_parse_timeout_s.description: Seconds a branch's own read and parse of a code lesson may take (waiting behind another parse in the process included), a share of the code plane's enrichment bound; past it the lesson is served as trunk last checked it.

memory_conflict_resolver_batch.description: Marked rows read per batch; a full batch with no errors is followed at once by the next, for up to memory_conflict_resolver_burst_seconds of a pass.

memory_conflict_resolver_burst_seconds.description: Seconds a pass whose owed read came back full keeps reading the next batch at once; a short read ends it. 0 = one batch a pass. At most half of memory_conflict_resolver_max_pass_seconds, so a pass ends before its deadline.

memory_conflict_resolver_cap_share.description: The share of a namespace's daily LLM cost cap the conflict resolver may spend, counted over its own calls; the rest stays for the requests.

memory_conflict_resolver_clear_confidenc.description: Below this confidence a verdict changes nothing. At or above it a compatible verdict clears the pair's flag.

memory_conflict_resolver_concurrency.description: Rows of a pass judged at once (LLM calls in flight). 1 judges them one at a time; doubling it roughly doubles the rows judged a minute, up to the provider's rate limit.

memory_conflict_resolver_enabled.description: The conflict resolver: a leader-only worker that judges each write marked for it (a live peer of its type at cosine >= memory_conflict_resolver_min_similarity, or flagged `conflicted`) against its nearest peers in one LLM call, then retires, flags or clears. Unset, it is resolved at load: off when the LLM provider or conflict_resolver_model's provider is `fake`, else on (without the key, writes are marked and judged once it is set); true / false force it. ~$0.005 per judged write on gpt-6.1-sol.

memory_conflict_resolver_flag_confidence.description: An update or a contradiction at or above this confidence acts: it flags the pair for review, or retires where the retire confidence and the policy allow; below it, it changes nothing. Between the clear confidence and the retire confidence.

memory_conflict_resolver_interval_second.description: Seconds the resolver waits after a pass before the next one; at least 1.

memory_conflict_resolver_max_attempts.description: Times a row is judged and left owed (a flagged peer the answer leaves out, an error after the call) before it is stamped, errored: each is a paid call.

memory_conflict_resolver_max_owed_age_da.description: Days a write stays owed a judgement: an owed row older than this is no longer judged, and stays as it was written.

memory_conflict_resolver_max_pass_second.description: Seconds a conflict-resolver pass may run before the supervisor abandons it.

memory_conflict_resolver_max_peers.description: Most peers judged with a row in one call, nearest first.

memory_conflict_resolver_min_similarity.description: Peers down to this cosine (same memory_type) mark a write for the resolver and join the cluster it is judged in. The cosine `conflicted` flag stays at the conflict threshold. A peer at this cosine or above can be an update of the row; below it, almost never.

memory_conflict_resolver_pause_after_sto.description: Seconds the resolver waits after a pass the model, the locks or a provider outage stopped, and a namespace whose rows got the same refusal row after row waits alone.

memory_conflict_resolver_recheck_batch.description: Rows already `conflicted` that no resolver judged (a cosine flag, or an older build's judge) re-checked per pass, after the marked rows. 0 = no re-check.

memory_conflict_resolver_recheck_idle_se.description: Seconds before the re-check of unjudged `conflicted` rows runs again once its read came back short; the read scans every `conflicted` row.

memory_conflict_resolver_retire_confiden.description: An update at or above this confidence retires the older row (auto_reinforce, newest_wins); one between the flag confidence and this is flagged for review.

memory_conflicts_count_ttl_s.description: Seconds a namespace's open-conflict count is cached between reads.

memory_coverage_sweep_gate_ttl_s.description: Seconds a namespace's coverage-sweep override is cached.

memory_decision_extract_known_max.description: Decisions already recorded from a document that a re-run lists and judges against the text; one past this many is never flagged or retired. 0 = none.

memory_decision_extract_restatement_top_.description: Closest decision keys a candidate is checked against for a pinned or attested restatement under another key (cosine only); the fetch caps at 500 rows.

memory_decision_extract_window_chars.description: Characters one extraction read takes: a shorter document is read whole, a longer one in windows of whole sections. Sized so a dense window's reply fits the decision_extract cap.

memory_durability_verifier_max_facts_per.description: One call judges at most this many facts; a longer capture is judged in slices (groups never span slices — a missed fold only keeps a paraphrase).

memory_embed_answer_topic.description: Prepend the extractor's `question_topic` to the embedded text of assistant-direct-answer facts, so a topic-only follow-up matches them. The stored value is untouched; takes effect on (re-)ingest.

memory_embeddings_patch_parts_probe_seco.description: Seconds a process caches its count of patch parts on loom.memory_embeddings (server/core/vectors/patch_parts.py); the fact leg reads quantized codes only while the count is zero.

memory_entity_extract_parse_fail_max.description: Consecutive unparseable model replies for one memory before the entity extractor stamps it failed and moves on.

memory_expiry_demote_factor.description: `demote` multiplies confidence by this factor, never below `memory_expiry_demote_floor`.

memory_expiry_demote_floor.description: Lowest confidence a `demote` (expiry or run.complete) leaves on a row.

memory_expiry_sweep_batch_size.description: Expired rows one sweep pass applies.

memory_expiry_sweep_enabled.description: Apply each expired row's `on_expire` (tombstone | demote | anonymize) as a version row. Reads already hide expired rows; the sweep records it.

memory_exposure_ledger_enabled.description: Read-side exposure ledger in loom.memory_exposures: one row per read (token subject, returned keys, query digest never the text, scope) plus an hourly per-actor roll-up. Carries no user content.

memory_extract_agent_learnings.description: Whether extraction files an assistant's rules about itself as learnings to review; a request can only turn it off. Turn on once every replica's build erases loom.learnings_supporters.

memory_extract_coding_sweep_min_user_tur.description: A coding capture keeps the coverage sweep's density / uncovered auto-gates only with at least this many user turns (on short sessions the sweep's output is mostly junk). 0 = always keep. An explicit namespace / per-call switch wins either way.

memory_extract_compact_prompt_max_chars.description: Current messages totalling at most this many characters are extracted with the compact system prompt (every rule, the schema anchors a short statement can match, no structured-answer block); longer ones keep the full prompt. 0 turns it off.

memory_extract_coverage_sweep_auto_min_s.description: With the namespace and the call silent, the coverage sweep still runs when the ingest is statement-dense — some turn holds at least this many statements (a fact list, a long update). 0 = never. Chatty conversation (one to four sentences a turn) never reaches it.

memory_extract_coverage_sweep_auto_min_u.description: With the namespace and the call silent and no list-shaped turn, a conversation ingest still gets the coverage sweep when the first pass left at least this many statements without a memory (lexical, LLM-free). 0 = never: on conversation the gate fires on nearly every session, so enabling it is the operator's token trade.

memory_extract_coverage_sweep_batch_item.description: The coverage sweep reads its listed turns and sentences in groups of this many items, one concurrent call each (more recall for more tokens). 0 = one call.

memory_extract_coverage_sweep_max_senten.description: Inside a turn the first pass cited, the individual statements no fact covers are swept too (a fact list, a long update), at most this many.

memory_extract_coverage_sweep_max_turns.description: Most uncovered turns one coverage sweep call reads; later ones are left out. 0 = no cap.

memory_extract_coverage_sweep_min_chars.description: Shortest turn, in characters, the coverage sweep reads; shorter "thanks!"-sized turns are skipped.

memory_extract_existing_short_limit.description: Existing memories (fact rows only) an extraction in the compact-prompt tier (`memory_extract_compact_prompt_max_chars`) sees for update detection (sized on an extraction eval); 0 lets it see the caller's full limit. A longer transcript sees none: shown the namespace's facts, the extractor links later details to them instead of writing them.

memory_extract_observation_date_default.description: The observation date a write is anchored to when the caller sends none. "request_time" = today's UTC date, so valid_at is never NULL for a live agent; "none" = undated.

memory_extract_size_segment_chars.description: Size segment windows also start past this many characters of message content, whatever the message count; a window closes early once its turns carry this much (an agent transcript with tool results runs ~190K chars a session at the median). 0 disables the character budget (turn budget only).

memory_extract_size_segment_max.description: Most size segment windows per session; past it the last window takes the remainder (windows grow past `memory_extract_size_segment_turns` turns first).

memory_extract_size_segment_messages.description: Size segments: a session longer than this many messages is extracted in fixed windows of `memory_extract_size_segment_turns` turns (a turn = one user message + the assistant replies that follow). 0 disables. One call per window, concurrently.

memory_extract_size_segment_turns.description: Turns per size segment window (a window never splits a turn).

memory_extract_value_updates.description: Value-update supersession on the extraction write path (memory.app.value_updates): a fresh memory restating an existing one with a different value token marks the older one superseded. Costs one ANN lookup per written row; a per-request `detect_updates` overrides it.

memory_extract_value_updates_min_cosine.description: Least cosine similarity a neighbour needs to be checked as the older value of a fresh memory; set below `conflict_threshold`.

memory_extract_verify_models.description: The durability check on a coding capture: one batched call per capture per listed model (CSV) judges each fact durable or not and folds same-claim paraphrases and replaced states. A fact is dropped only when every model says drop; folds come from the first. Fails open. "" turns it off.

memory_extract_verify_timeout_s.description: Seconds one durability-check call (`memory_extract_verify_models`) may take; a timeout keeps every fact.

memory_facts_projection_wait_s.description: Seconds facts.traverse waits, when it starts, for the graph projections of its namespace still in flight in this process and the others.

memory_facts_traverse_ttl_s.description: Seconds a facts.traverse result is reused for the same walk.

memory_for_file_whole_tokens.description: Tokens (4 characters each) memory.for_file gives its decision and constraint rows, which print whole outside token_budget; a row past it is left out and named.

memory_harm_reinforcement_weight.description: Recall-equivalents one `harm` event (a relied-on row in a run that ended badly) subtracts. Floored at the write-time base: harm cancels earned reinforcement, never ranks below cosine and never deletes. None = the `used` weight; 0 = counted in memory.health, not charged.

memory_list_viewer_limit.description: memory.list rows per call for a token below writer on the namespace; it pages with `offset` (wire cap stays 1000). 0 = no viewer cap.

memory_namespace_health_failure_ttl_s.description: Seconds a failed namespace-health lookup is remembered (never longer than namespace_health_ttl_seconds), so the context pack does not re-run failing reads on every call.

memory_namespace_retrieval_defaults_ttl_.description: Seconds a namespace's retrieval defaults are cached; a change reaches search within it.

memory_negative_demote_threshold.description: Negative memory.outcome signals after which a memory is quarantined (status 'rejected', excluded from search). 0 = off: negatives stay audit-only.

memory_observe_extract_session_context_l.description: The most observations a session's notes read: the notes prompt is bounded by characters anyway; this bounds the read.

memory_pending_disclosure_ttl_s.description: Seconds the pending-extraction count a read discloses is cached.

memory_prior_cap.description: Cap on memory.search's metadata priors (confidence, soft tag/category) so they break ties instead of re-ranking. 0.0 = uncapped; a request's `prior_cap` overrides it.

memory_profile_cas_max_retries.description: Attempts a profile write makes when a concurrent write moved the profile under it.

memory_profile_search_embed_cap.description: The most sections one search embeds on the fly.

memory_proposals_policy_ttl_s.description: Seconds a namespace's proposal policy is cached; a change applies within it.

memory_proposals_scan_cap.description: A listing reads at most this many proposals before `only` / `limit` — the graded counts are one statement over them; a namespace holding more on trial than this is a queue nobody is deciding, not a page.

memory_quality_actor_names.description: Comma-separated names of the people whose sessions this deployment records ("jane,jane doe"). The junk-fact filters read "Jane ran a command …" like "The user ran a command …". Empty = only the generic actors (user, assistant, Claude, the agent).

memory_quality_peer_host_pattern.description: Regex (case-insensitive) matching the host name of another agent session on this deployment ("build-[0-9]+"); a fact whose subject is such a peer is coordination chatter, not a durable fact. Empty = no host pattern.

memory_query_nodes_enabled.description: Past queries as nodes: one loom.query_nodes row per memory.search (normalised text, embedding, returned keys), gated on the namespace's capture consent; the erasure saga deletes the table.

memory_reinforcement_closer_cache_second.description: Seconds one (org, consumer) closer answer is cached per worker.

memory_reinforcement_closer_window_days.description: Days a consumer's closer keeps its run-less reads credited.

memory_repo_decisions_timeout_s.description: Seconds loom_search's read of the scoped repository's decisions may take; a slower read adds nothing and the memory section serves the home search alone.

memory_retrieval_empty_block_retries.description: Retries of a vector read that ClickHouse answers with an empty-block error (code 10 on a part still being written) before the search fails.

memory_retrieval_empty_block_retry_sleep.description: Seconds before the first retry of an empty retrieval block (`memory_retrieval_empty_block_retries`); each later one waits one more step of it.

memory_rrf_code_shape_lo.description: RRF adaptive lexical weight: code/path-shaped queries (CamelCase, extensions, separators, digit runs) down-weight the lexical leg so fusion leans semantic; prose keeps full weight. Shape at/below which w_lex == 1.0 (prose).

memory_rrf_lexical_weight_floor.description: Least weight the RRF adaptive lexical weight gives the lexical leg on a code-shaped query, so it is never fully zeroed.

memory_run_complete_retain.description: What run.complete does to the rows the run wrote when the call does not say: keep = nothing; demote = scale confidence by the expiry demote factor now; expire = expires_at now + memory_run_complete_expire_days with on_expire=demote. Pinned, verified, promoted, locked, episodic and reflection rows are always kept, and so is everything an MCP session's implicit run wrote when the transport closes it.

memory_scratchpad_max_chars.description: Characters each injected working-memory block renders before it is cut with "(truncated)".

memory_search_abstain_threshold.description: Top-hit similarity below which a search abstains (weak abstention): the scalar gate for fake embedders or LOOM_ADAPTIVE_THRESHOLDS=false; a calibrated namespace or embedder derives its own.

memory_search_abstain_top_sim_scope.description: Which cosine the abstain gate reads: "first" = the fused rank-1 row, "window" = the best cosine among returned rows.

memory_search_asserted_boost_scale.description: Tie-break boost (cosine units) for a hand-asserted fact row (source_class 'asserted', not a hint:/procedure/summary:/obs: row) against derived rows; never a lever over a stronger match. 0 disables.

memory_search_bm25_live_tail.description: bm25_hybrid merges the once-a-minute BM25 roll-ups with a live aggregate over rows newer than their mark, so df and corpus size are exact. Off = roll-ups alone (up to ~70 s behind a write).

memory_search_chunk_date_source.description: How memory.search dates a chunk: "session" by its conversation's digest, "parent" by the session's first fact anchor.

memory_search_chunk_min_share.description: Smallest window share verbatim chunks keep when the pool has them. 0.0 = off.

memory_search_default_mode.description: search_mode used when the caller sets neither search_mode nor a recipe. The wire default stays "rrf"; planner shape rules still apply on top.

memory_search_default_namespace_scope.description: Default `namespace_scope` when a request leaves it unset. "this" reads the addressed namespace only; "all_mine" also reads the caller's own namespaces (the MCP loom_search asks for it by name), see docs/concepts/identities-and-namespaces.md#reading-several-namespaces.

memory_search_digest_descent_k.description: Facts digest descent adds as candidates from each expanded session.

memory_search_digest_descent_top_m.description: Top session digests in the pool that digest descent expands: a digest among them adds its session's top facts as candidates (+300 ms ask p50); MemorySearchInput.digest_descent overrides.

memory_search_embed_bound_retries.description: Retries of a query embedding after a timed-out first attempt, each bounded by `memory_search_embed_bound_s`.

memory_search_embed_bound_s.description: Per-attempt bound (seconds) on the query embedding; after the retries the search answers 503 EMBED_TIMEOUT. 0 = unbounded.

memory_search_entity_boost_max_pairs.description: Most (entity, memory_key) edges the entity-boost lookup expands to.

memory_search_entity_boost_top_entities.description: Entity-boost candidate shape (server/memory/app/search/ann_entity_boosts.py). loom.entity_vectors holds one row per (entity, memory_key) edge, so the lookup ranks distinct entities first, then expands to edges (a flat LIMIT surfaced as few as 1 distinct entity). Distinct entities the lookup keeps; `memory_search_entity_boost_max_pairs` bounds the edge expansion (a hub can carry hundreds), which bounds work rather than results.

memory_search_entity_summaries_top_n.description: Pre-built entity summaries memory.search's entity-summary leg fetches per namespace.

memory_search_excerpt_bodies_k.description: Above this top_k a search that pinned no `bodies` serves excerpts, and per-hit explanation / score_components ride only under `explain: true`. Keys, order and scores are unchanged. 0 = never.

memory_search_excerpt_chars.description: Body length (chars) for bodies="excerpt" (the MCP search default); a decision or constraint row keeps its stored excerpt.

memory_search_fact_codes_fetch_multiplie.description: Over-fetch of the codes pass on the main leg; x1 is too low (it changes the top-10 on a quarter of queries).

memory_search_fact_codes_first.description: Codes-first main fact leg (`vector_search_use_quantized_codes = 1`), safe only while loom.memory_embeddings has no patch part (ClickHouse skips the lazy rescore under patch parts). "auto" follows a 60 s system.parts probe (gauge loom.memory_embeddings.patch_parts); "on" / "off" pin it. The setting ships only where the replica probe finds it.

memory_search_fact_leg_max_threads.description: `max_threads` pin on the main fact statement; 0 = no pin (threads follow the marks); 4 bounds each statement to four threads. Unpinned costs more CPU and peak memory per statement.

memory_search_fallback_max_llm_calls.description: LLM calls one fallback round may spend before further ones are denied.

memory_search_fallback_max_rounds.description: Recursive rounds the fallback cascade (iterative-judge retry) may run; it stops at this or `memory_search_fallback_max_wall_ms`, whichever trips first. The first-pass retrieve always runs.

memory_search_fallback_max_vector_querie.description: Vector queries one fallback round may issue before further ones are denied.

memory_search_fallback_max_wall_ms.description: Wall-clock ms the fallback cascade may spend across all rounds before it stops.

memory_search_fanout_kinds.description: Namespace kinds an all_mine fan-out spans (memory.search, conversation.search, MCP loom_search; knowledge.search reads knowledge_search_fanout_kinds): comma list over loom.namespaces.kind; a namespace with no kind row stays; "" = every kind. Code and QA indexes are reached by name or their own tools (measured sweep of 24 namespaces: 6.2 s).

memory_search_fanout_max_namespaces.description: Upper bound on how many of the caller's namespaces an all_mine fan-out reads besides the addressed one; a search names the rest in `namespaces_skipped`. Every memory leg issues at least one statement per namespace. A guard, not a tuning knob: set well above what one person holds, so it bounds a runaway sweep rather than trimming normal ones.

memory_search_floor_mode.description: Sub-floor handling when the caller sets top_k: "readmit" (fill k, tag below_floor), "ids_only" (fill k with empty bodies), "drop". A request's floor_mode overrides.

memory_search_graph_seed.description: What seeds memory.search's graph leg: "query", "recent" or "both". Under recent or both, the entities of the identity's newest memories (`memory_search_graph_seed_recent_memories`) join the query's seeds.

memory_search_graph_seed_recent_max.description: Most recent-memory entities added to the graph seeds under recent/both.

memory_search_graph_seed_recent_memories.description: Newest memories of the identity whose entities seed the graph under recent/both.

memory_search_hyde_fallback_threshold.description: No-probe fallback for the question→fact P25 gate (≈ P25 for text-embedding-3-small): the loom_search precision floor and calibration.get's scalar row read it.

memory_search_hyde_timeout_s.description: Seconds the HyDE model call may take before the search embeds the query itself.

memory_search_identifier_grounding.description: Identifier-grounding abstain: when the query carries a salient identifier (PR/issue number, test id, @handle) and no returned hit contains any of them, abstain with abstain_code "entity_absent" regardless of the top cosine — catches the on-topic but wrong neighbour the cosine gate cannot.

memory_search_identifier_grounding_max_t.description: The grounding leg applies only to queries of at most this many whitespace tokens; longer inputs (a PR body, a path list) carry incidental numbers. 0 = no cap.

memory_search_key_axis.description: Key-embedding axis on the fact leg: "on" scores least(value_dist, key_dist) and reads both vector columns (measured 399 vs 203 MB/query on a 30k-row namespace); "off" reads the value vector only; "auto" turns it on per namespace when its key-reuse share is at or above memory_search_key_axis_auto_reuse_share (cached for memory_search_key_axis_auto_ttl_seconds; a failed probe reads as off). A per-request `key_axis` wins.

memory_search_key_axis_auto_reuse_share.description: "auto" key-axis threshold: share of a namespace's keys written more than once. 0.05 sits between product namespaces and chat namespaces.

memory_search_key_axis_auto_ttl_seconds.description: Seconds a namespace's "auto" key-axis probe result is cached before it is re-read.

memory_search_key_match_boost_scale.description: Boost (cosine units) of a full-strength key match: a tie-break inside the pool's band, not a lever over it (a 0.5 scale lifted wrong rows over gold).

memory_search_key_match_min_strength.description: A key matches when it covers at least this share of the query's idf-weighted stems (idf over the namespace's own keys).

memory_search_key_match_mode.description: When the key-match arm runs: "always" (every search; measured 585-781 ms p50 on live namespaces), "gated" (only when an added row could reach the served window: rrf/rerank pool, pool short of top_k, an under-covered identifier, or a pooled key already matching), "off".

memory_search_max_pool_top_k.description: Upper bound on the first-stage pool size; a caller's top_k above it raises the bound to top_k.

memory_search_min_similarity.description: Cosine floor: hits below it are dropped as noise (ANN always returns top_k). The backstop when rerank is bypassed or fails.

memory_search_page_ttl_s.description: Seconds a parked page (a `paging=true` search's tail) stays fetchable before the TTL merge reclaims it.

memory_search_per_key_cap.description: Rows of one memory_key kept by the final block, key-match and the entity follow (0 = no cap; the first two keep all for aggregational/temporal_diff), and one-per-key callers' over-fetch.

memory_search_pool_multiplier_deep.description: A deep-budget search's pool multiplier (the budget class `deep`).

memory_search_pool_multiplier_rerank.description: Rerank gets the widest pool: a reranker only reorders what the first stage surfaced (measured: items it should promote sat at rank 11-30). Affects rerank-enabled searches only.

memory_search_pool_multiplier_standard.description: First-stage pool = top_k × multiplier, per retrieval profile, capped at memory_search_max_pool_top_k (all_mine searches multiply by namespace and sub-query count).

memory_search_preference_fallback.description: Boost for any preference-typed/tagged row on any query; 0.0 makes it intent-gated (only a query naming the attribute earns +0.3).

memory_search_private_first_stop_similar.description: Visibility-ordered private-first fallback (non-scoped tokens): the best private-namespace similarity that skips the public pass. "Private" is namespace visibility, not the caller's role; scoped tokens use their priority order instead.

memory_search_quality_pool_multiplier.description: Pool widening factor for a quality-filtered search (loom_search, context.pack), applied before junk is dropped.

memory_search_query_rewrite_threshold.description: No-probe fallback for the query-rewrite gate the calibration reports (calibration.get's scalar row): ≈ question→fact P10 for text-embedding-3-small.

memory_search_query_spelling_max_words.description: A query of at most this many words embeds each all-lowercase word of 4+ letters in the identifier spelling the caller's rows in the addressed namespace use most ("datalakecatalog" -> "DataLakeCatalog"; never "what" -> "What"). One read of the namespace beside the embed (100-300 ms for 40k rows), reused for a minute; fail-open. 0 = off.

memory_search_recency_pool_weight.description: Recency-intent searches ("latest", "current …") re-rank the fused pool by date: the newest dated hit gains this much, the oldest and undated hits nothing. 0.0 = off. A namespace can set its own in retrieval_defaults.

memory_search_reinforcement_half_life_da.description: Days after which a use's reinforcement weighs half: the base half-life, which grows with a row's use count.

memory_search_reinforcement_weight.description: Weight of the decayed-reinforcement rank term (recalls and positive memory.outcome signals, fading with time since last reinforcement). 0 disables; the term is capped below relevance.

memory_search_rerank_timeout_s.description: Seconds memory.search's reranker endpoint (a named endpoint of rerank_endpoints_json, or builtin:cohere) may take to answer; past it the search keeps its input order and says so in `degraded`. builtin:openai is an LLM call and waits llm_request_timeout_s.

memory_search_sensitivity_demote.description: Additive penalty on rows tagged `sensitivity:medium|high` unless the query has contact intent. 0.0 disables.

memory_search_set_chunk_rows.description: How many of a writer's served rows of one key, those with the newest vectors, a pooled memory.set chunk is matched against, by value, to find the row it was cut from.

memory_search_set_expansion_leg_top_k.description: Set-expansion instance legs (collective nouns -> "has a sister"): each phrase runs as a narrow sub-query leg of this many rows; a row joins only above `memory_search_set_expansion_min_similarity`, at most `memory_search_set_expansion_max_added` per search, never above the main leg's best row.

memory_search_set_expansion_max_added.description: Most rows the set-expansion legs add to one search.
