memory_search_set_expansion_min_similari.description: Similarity a set-expansion leg's row must exceed to join the pool.

memory_search_source_class_boost_eligibl.description: Comma list of source_class values whose rows may earn the user-derived rank terms (preference, prior group, reinforcement); "" = every row. Leaving out "extracted" keeps an inference from outranking a statement by its priors.

memory_search_spelling_lookup_timeout_s.description: Seconds the query-spelling lookup may take; it reads every row of the namespace it may read (100-300 ms server-side for 40k rows) and overlaps the embed on a cache miss.

memory_search_tier_stop_similarity.description: Tier waterfall stop: a per-tier best similarity at or above this stops the search before lower-priority tiers. A control cutoff, not a return filter (memory_search_min_similarity still gates rows); keep it above the noise band (~0.10-0.25) or a middling hit hides a stronger one.

memory_search_top_k_ceiling_viewer.description: Per-token top_k ceiling by the token's role on the namespace: viewer and writer each have one, admin and above are uncapped. 0 = no ceiling. The applied ceiling rides the response as `top_k_ceiling` and the ledger as `out_top_k_ceiling`.

memory_search_top_k_ceiling_writer.description: top_k ceiling for a writer token on the namespace; 0 = no ceiling.

memory_search_trust_weight.description: Weight on the provenance term (source_class + verified); 0 = off, a strict no-op in every mode.

memory_sensitive_on_expire.description: `on_expire` given to a sensitive row whose caller set none.

memory_sensitive_retention_days.description: `medium`/`high` rows get expires_at = now + N days on the set and bulk paths (a shorter caller expiry wins) and, if the caller set none, this on_expire. 0 = off.

memory_sensitivity_autodetect.description: With no explicit `sensitivity`, detect it from the value with regexes: credential shapes, card numbers, SSNs and stated PINs -> 'high' (never embedded, key-only reads, audited); email/phone/IBAN -> 'medium' (embedded, labelled). Off = every row stays ''.

memory_session_digest_max_input_chars.description: Transcript characters the session-digest call reads (~4 chars a token); 0 = the built-in 3000.

memory_set_chunk_max_chunks.description: Max chunks per memory.set value (48 ≈ 34 KB); the tail is recorded in loom.memory_drops as chunk.split/truncated.

memory_structured_answer_excerpt_limit.description: content_excerpt ceiling for answer-bearing facts (question_topic set) when memory_capture_structured_answers is on, so an enumerated answer is not clipped mid-list; every other fact keeps EXCERPT_LIMIT (1,200 chars).

memory_summary_entity_ttl_s.description: Seconds the entity vocabulary of a namespace's summaries is cached for the summary read leg.

memory_usage_fold_acted_max_rows_per_pas.description: Most exposure rows one usage-fold pass reads to credit acted-on memories; the watermark holds until a pass drains below it.

memory_usage_fold_max_memories_per_pass.description: Most memories one usage-fold pass folds.

memory_usage_fold_max_pending_mutations.description: Backpressure: a pass is skipped — watermark untouched — while the destination table already carries this many unfinished mutations on the connected replica. Every lightweight UPDATE is a patch part plus a Keeper log entry; enough of them pending on a large table can expire replicas' Keeper sessions and leave them read-only.

memory_usage_fold_pass_time_budget_s.description: Seconds one usage-fold pass may run before it stops and leaves the rest to the next.

memory_used_cited_reinforcement_weight.description: Recall-equivalents one `used_cited` event (memory.ask crediting the keys its answer cited) adds; `used` stays for labels an agent wrote. None = the `used` weight; 0 = recorded, not ranking.

memory_used_reinforcement_weight.description: Recall-equivalents one `used` event (run.complete memories_used, memory.outcome "used") adds to search-side reinforcement; the boost follows use, not exposure. 0 = recorded, not reinforcing.

memory_value_advisory_chars.description: A searchable memory.set value serializing longer than this many chars gets one advisory line (the write still lands): only the first EXCERPT_LIMIT chars are embedded, and past the embedder's 8,191-token cap nothing is. 30,000 chars ≈ 8k tokens. 0 disables.

memory_webhook_ack_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds a memory webhook receiver has to answer a POST (the name lookup, the connection and the status line) before it counts as failed; also the registration's lookup limit.

memory_webhook_allow_http.description: True lets a memory webhook use plain http (a local receiver in development); false: https only.

memory_webhook_backoff_steps_seconds.description: Comma-separated seconds a failed memory webhook event waits before each retry, one step per failed attempt; every step over 0.

memory_webhook_cooldown_seconds.description: Seconds of a memory webhook's first cooldown; each one after it doubles, up to memory_webhook_max_cooldown_seconds.

memory_webhook_deliver_concurrency.description: Memory webhook POSTs one delivery pass has in flight at once (one per webhook at most).

memory_webhook_deliver_enabled.description: Deliver the signed memory-change events of loom.memory_webhook_outbox to each namespace's registered webhooks (the memory_webhook_deliver worker).

memory_webhook_deliver_idle_interval_sec.description: Seconds between memory webhook delivery passes that found nothing due.

memory_webhook_deliver_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between memory webhook delivery passes while events are going out.

memory_webhook_deliver_max_pass_seconds.description: Seconds a memory webhook delivery pass may run before the supervisor abandons it (at least 30).

memory_webhook_deliver_reserve_seconds.description: Seconds before the pass deadline a memory webhook delivery pass stops its POSTs, kept for the insert after them; less than memory_webhook_deliver_max_pass_seconds.

memory_webhook_failures_before_cooldown.description: Failed POSTs in a row after which the delivery worker passes a memory webhook over for a cooldown (kept per process; a 2xx resets it).

memory_webhook_lease_margin_seconds.description: Seconds past memory_webhook_deliver_max_pass_seconds a memory webhook event a pass leased stays passed over by other passes, so a crashed pass's events come back after it.

memory_webhook_max_attempts.description: POSTs per memory webhook event before it is marked dead; the 2.75-day delivery deadline marks it dead sooner whatever this is.

memory_webhook_max_backoff_seconds.description: Seconds a failed memory webhook event waits at most: caps each backoff step and is the wait after the last.

memory_webhook_max_cooldown_seconds.description: Seconds a memory webhook's cooldown grows to at most.

memory_webhook_max_per_namespace.description: Live memory webhooks a namespace may hold: every memory write inserts one outbox row per webhook that takes its event.

memory_webhook_max_posts_per_pass.description: Due memory webhook events one delivery pass POSTs at most; the rest go next pass.

memory_webhook_posts_per_webhook.description: Events of one memory webhook a delivery pass POSTs at most, so every webhook with work gets its turn.

memory_webhook_private_hosts.description: Comma-separated hostnames or IP literals, no port (exact, any case; an IDN in either spelling) a memory webhook may reach although they resolve to a private, loopback or link-local address; "" = none.

memory_webhook_refresh_seconds.description: Seconds between each process's reads of the registered memory webhooks; a webhook registered or removed on another process applies to writes here within it.

memory_webhook_removal_window_leases.description: Leases (max pass plus lease margin each) after a webhook.remove in which delivery passes still mark the removed memory webhook's events dead.

memory_write_candidate_batch.description: Facts per batched candidate lookup (conflict and value-update peers) on the write path; matches the per-fact concurrency so wall time stays flat. 0 = one statement per fact.

mentor_max_hints_per_session.description: At most this many hints per session, each code once.

mentor_ttl_seconds.description: Seconds a per-process (org, namespace, agent) mentor profile is cached (a failed read ≤ 300 s). 0 disables the mentor everywhere (no pack section, no call hints, empty mentor.brief).

migrate_mutation_wait_s.description: Seconds a migration file waits for the mutations it started (MATERIALIZE, UPDATE, a column type change) to finish on every replica; past it the file fails unrecorded.

model_calls_off_drop_per_pass.description: Waiting requests of a switched-off org one extraction-queue pass drops; the rest go on the next pass.

model_calls_off_max_wait_days.description: Days a switched-off org's queued requests (the extraction queue) wait, from when the org was switched off, before they are dropped, each with a memory_drops record. 1 to 29: the queue's own 30-day TTL would otherwise remove them first, with no record.

model_calls_policy_max_stale_seconds.description: Seconds a process trusts its copy of the org model-call switch, and of the extraction policies, when it cannot read it again; past it, every model call for an org is refused and no extraction runs (fail closed). 15 to 300.

model_calls_policy_refresh_seconds.description: Seconds between each process's reads of the orgs whose model calls are switched off (loom.org_model_calls) and of the operators' extraction policies (loom.extraction_policies); a change reaches every process within it.

namespace_audit_index_row_scan_cap.description: Most live rows the namespace audit's value scan reads (it is O(total value bytes)); above it that check is skipped and says so.

namespace_autoregister_enabled.description: A principal's first write into a namespace with no loom.namespaces row inserts one: owner = token subject (none on a name already in use), `kind = 'bench'` under a bench prefix, `retention_days = 0` (never a TTL). No ALTER.

namespace_autoregister_skip_prefixes.description: Op-name prefixes the auto-register hook ignores: ops on a namespace rather than into it, the code plane (registers `kind = 'code'` itself), and the operator planes.

namespace_bench_prefixes.description: Comma-separated name prefixes of throwaway harness namespaces: stamped `kind = 'bench'` by `namespace.register` (when no kind is given) and auto-register, and scanned by `namespaces-gc`.

namespace_gc_batch.description: Namespaces one erasure saga purges, oldest write first (at least 1).

namespace_gc_idle_hours.description: Hours without a write before a bench namespace is purged.

namespace_gc_sagas_per_pass.description: Erasure sagas one GC pass submits (at least 1).

namespace_gc_worker_enabled.description: namespace_gc: `kind = 'bench'` namespaces with live memory and no write for `namespace_gc_idle_hours` are purged by one list-scoped erasure saga per batch, at most `namespace_gc_sagas_per_pass` a pass, kept to loom tables.

namespace_health_ttl_seconds.description: Seconds a namespace's health summary is cached per process (a failed lookup at most `memory_namespace_health_failure_ttl_s`). 0 disables the summary and its pack section.

namespace_ontology_cardinality_ttl_s.description: Seconds a namespace's relation cardinalities (one or many) are cached for the triple writer.

namespace_report_hash_max_bytes.description: Largest value (bytes) namespace.audit, namespace.validate and memory.inspect read to cite a row's content hash; a larger row is cited with none. 0 = cite no hash.

namespace_taxonomy_ttl_s.description: Seconds a namespace's taxonomy is reused: one is four FINAL scans of the namespace (about 20 MB per open on a large namespace) and changes only when the namespace does.

namespace_tune_document_sample.description: Most live documents namespace.tune re-chunks in process to judge the chunk size and stride, picked by a hash of their source_uri; the report states the cap.

namespace_write_marks_flush_interval_s.description: loom.namespace_write_marks is an in-process max per (org, namespace, plane), flushed as one INSERT this often.

oauth_access_token_ttl_seconds.description: Lifetime of an OAuth access token, in seconds; at most a day, which bounds access after the IdP deactivates someone (only a refresh asks it).

oauth_enabled.description: MCP one-click connect: dynamic client registration and /oauth/authorize on top of the sign-in routes (device grant, token, revoke) every auth-on deployment serves. Opt-in: anyone can register a client.

oauth_issuer.description: Public base URL used in OAuth discovery and redirects; empty derives it from each request. Required when `oauth_login_provider` is "oidc" (the IdP callback URL is built from it).

oauth_login_provider.description: How people sign in (dashboard, `loom login`, MCP connect): "password" (Loom's own form) or "oidc" (the external IdP; loom maps the verified email to an account and still mints its own token). "oidc" closes password sign-in and self-signup, and requires `oauth_issuer` and the three oidc_* values.

oauth_signin_state_sweep_interval_second.description: Seconds between passes of the always-on sweep that drops sign-in state (loom.oauth_signin_state keys) past its credential's expiry.

observe_extract_buffer_chars.description: Buffer threshold: a session whose un-distilled observations reach this many characters is distilled even without an explicit observe.crystallize, like a short-term buffer that flushes when full. 0 disables; the READY tag still works either way.

observe_extract_buffer_min_observations.description: Observations a session needs before the buffer threshold can fire (at least 1); a per-namespace value wins.

observe_extract_enabled.description: Deferred-extraction worker for the observe plane: distills READY rows (observe.record/crystallize) into durable memories through the memory.set_from_messages pipeline. Off by default (makes LLM calls).

observe_extract_max_events_per_session.description: Most transition events written per distilled session.

observe_extract_max_pass_seconds.description: Seconds an observe-extract pass may run before the supervisor abandons it.

observe_extract_notes_min_observations.description: A session's procedure and hint (observe notes) are mined only once the session holds this many non-trivial observations. 0 = any.

observe_skip_tools.description: Tool names (case-insensitive globs, comma-separated) whose observations are stored content-less and already distilled: loom's own MCP tools (observing one copies a memory outside the key the user can delete) and the harness's meta tools, which say nothing about the task. "" disables the skip.

oidc_backchannel_base_url.description: Origin used for server-side sign-in calls to the issuer, preserving its Host header. Empty uses the issuer directly; browser redirects and bot-trust key fetches are unchanged.

oidc_client_id.description: Client id registered at the IdP; also the audience each id_token must carry.

oidc_issuer.description: External IdP issuer URL; its `/.well-known/openid-configuration` must name the same issuer.

oidc_jit_email_domains.description: Comma-separated email domains JIT provisioning admits; empty admits any verified email.

oidc_jit_org.description: Org that JIT-provisioned accounts are created in; required when `oidc_jit_provision` is on.

oidc_jit_provision.description: JIT provisioning: a first OIDC sign-in with no account creates a personal namespace in oidc_jit_org instead of being rejected. Off = fail closed. oidc_jit_email_domains (comma-separated) restricts it; empty admits any verified email the IdP authenticates.

openai_base_url.description: OpenAI's API root, for chat and embeddings: point it at an OpenAI-compatible inference gateway in front of OpenAI (its /v1 root).

ops_op_mix_min_writes.description: Writes in the `op_mix` check's window before its update-share warning can fire.

ops_op_mix_reads_per_write_warn.description: Reads per write above which the `op_mix` check warns (polling load).

ops_op_mix_update_share_warn.description: Share of writes that are updates below which the `op_mix` check warns (append-only bank).

ops_op_mix_window_days.description: Days of ops the `op_mix` check of ops.health reads: the create/read/update/delete mix over them warns when reads per write exceed `ops_op_mix_reads_per_write_warn` (polling load) or, after `ops_op_mix_min_writes`, the update share falls below `ops_op_mix_update_share_warn` (append-only bank).

ops_procedure_plane_min_packs.description: Context packs in the `procedure_plane` check's window before "no pack showed a procedure" can warn.

ops_procedure_plane_min_pairs.description: Pairs the `procedure_plane` check measures success retention over before its warning can fire.

ops_procedure_plane_retention_warn.description: Success retention (fraction) below which the `procedure_plane` check warns.

ops_procedure_plane_window_days.description: Days the `procedure_plane` check of ops.health reads: it warns when ≥ `ops_procedure_plane_min_packs` packs flowed and none showed a procedure while procedures exist, or when success retention over ≥ `ops_procedure_plane_min_pairs` pairs is below `ops_procedure_plane_retention_warn`.

orphan_vector_reconcile_enabled.description: Re-emit, with a tombstone, vector rows still live after their loom.memory row was tombstoned or erased, so search stops offering them. Bounded per pass; loom.integrity.orphan_vectors should read 0 between passes.

orphan_vector_reconcile_grace_seconds.description: Seconds before an unmatched embedding counts as orphaned, so a write whose two rows land apart is not taken for a deletion.

orphan_vector_reconcile_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between orphan vector reconcile passes.

orphan_vector_reconcile_max_keys_per_pas.description: Orphaned keys one pass re-emits tombstones for (at least 1).

otel_agent_labels_max_namespaces.description: Max namespaces `loom.memory.agent_labels_24h` names per probe (top N by label total); the rest sum under `loom.namespace = "other"`. 0 = no cap.

otel_census_scope.description: Who takes the whole-table censuses (invariants, code-plane counts, retention, agent labels, storage): "leader" = only the supervisor-lease holder, "process" = every process (costly).

otel_code_counts_cache_s.description: Seconds between refreshes of the per-namespace code-plane COUNT gauges (one FINAL scan each of code_files, code_chunks, code_symbols and code_edges, on the lease holder). The counts move once an index run, so an hour is enough; each refresh reads every live code row. 0 = every export.

otel_code_grep_replay_cache_s.description: Seconds between recounts of the code.grep wrong-abstain gauge (a `content` scan per namespace with abstains). 0 = gauge off.

otel_enabled.description: Master switch for OTel emission. `init_otel()` also refuses under pytest regardless: server/main.py calls it at import, and a test run must never ship rows into production observability tables.

otel_environment.description: The OTel resource `deployment.environment.name` stamped on every span, log and metric.

otel_excluded_urls.description: Comma-separated path regexes the FastAPI instrumentation opens no span for (health polls). "" = instrument every path but the sign-in routes (/oauth/), which are always left out: their URLs carry codes.

otel_exporter.description: OTel exporter, for spans and metrics: "ch" writes to `otel_traces` and `otel_metrics_*` in `clickstack_database` (`default` when empty) on the same service, "otlp" ships to otel_exporter_otlp_endpoint (headers: comma-separated K=V), "" = auto (otlp when the endpoint is set, else ch).

otel_exporter_otlp_endpoint.description: OTLP/HTTP collector base URL (`/v1/traces` and `/v1/metrics` are appended); set with `otel_exporter` = "", it selects the otlp exporter.

otel_gauge_heartbeat_s.description: Write a gauge point only when its value changed or this many seconds after the last write; 0 = every export. The ClickHouse exporter only (LOOM_OTEL_EXPORTER=ch); OTLP exports every point. Off because gauge tiles fill gaps with 0 and would draw a sawtooth.

otel_invariants_probe_s.description: Seconds between the state probe's whole-table readings (embed backlog, integrity invariants), taken on the lease holder only. The invariants read 0 and exist to catch drift, so an hour is enough; each reading is one FINAL pass over memory, memory_embeddings and entity_vectors.

otel_metrics_delta_temporality.description: Delta temporality for counters and histograms (an idle synchronous series writes no row). Off: the dashboards (deploy/hyperdx_dashboards.md) read cumulative rows — flip together with them.

otel_metrics_export_interval_s.description: Metric export cadence, seconds. Spans keep their own 3 s batch delay, which bounds span loss at SIGTERM.

otel_retention_census_s.description: Seconds between retention censuses (`loom.retention.*`: per-org counts over 7- and 45-day windows; one FINAL pass over loom.memory on the lease holder). 0 = every export.

otel_service_name.description: The OTel resource `service.name` stamped on every span, log and metric.

password_link_ttl_seconds.description: Seconds a password set-up link stays valid, at most a week (it sets a password once).

pg_admission_deadline_ms.description: Milliseconds a memory.set or memory.bulk_set keeps re-reaching its verdict while writes commit in its namespace (each round adds only those writes) before answering 503 ADMISSION_CONTENDED: the bound on how far a namespace's admissions may queue.

pg_admission_gap_rows.description: Revisions committed in a write's namespace during its check that its commit reads to clear them; a longer gap sends the write back to its check.

pg_admission_help_rows.description: Revisions a waiting admission publishes itself for a writer that stopped before publishing them; the delivery worker publishes the rest.

pg_admission_recent_vectors.description: Vectors of this process's recent writes kept to rule out a commit landing in another write's check without reading ClickHouse.

pg_admission_rounds.description: Passes a writer that reads its heads again makes when a key's head keeps changing between its read and its commit. Past them a write request answers 503 ADMISSION_CONTENDED; memory.consolidate and a background writer leave the keys for their next pass.

pg_backlog_count_cap.description: The most deliveries one backlog reading counts per source (`loom.pg.backlog`, health's `postgres.backlog`); past it the reading stops counting and says so (`capped`).

pg_backlog_health_cache_seconds.description: Seconds each process keeps its own backlog reading for `GET /v1/health?include=postgres`.

pg_commit_lock_timeout_ms.description: Milliseconds a memory commit or a `memory.redact` waits for a lock (its namespace's generation, which an erasure of the scope holds while it runs) before answering a retryable 503, so a long erasure does not hold every pooled connection it blocks; also how long a read that judges a head once it settles (a write whose commit answer was lost, a sensitivity relabel's close of its owed facts, by the sweep or the projection repair) waits on each head's lock.

pg_delivery_batch_rows.description: Deliveries one pass of each delivery worker publishes; also the expired deletion evidence and settled knowledge deliveries one pass sweeps.

pg_delivery_enabled.description: Background delivery of committed memory revisions and knowledge documents a request did not publish (the pg_delivery and knowledge_pg_delivery workers).

pg_delivery_idle_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between delivery passes that found nothing.

pg_delivery_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between delivery passes while there is work.

pg_delivery_lease_seconds.description: Seconds the delivery workers hold a memory revision's or a knowledge document's delivery before another may take it; also how long the conflict resolver sets aside a row whose flagged peer is not yet in ClickHouse.

pg_delivery_max_attempts.description: Times a delivery is tried before it is parked: a search document it cannot build is published as a stub for the embedding worker; a memory row ClickHouse keeps refusing is left out of claims and of its namespace's watermark, and counted in /v1/health?include=postgres (`postgres.parked_deliveries`). An audit row waiting in the outbox (a row an erasure moved there, or one a claim deferred because the holder it replaced may still insert it) is parked the same way (`postgres.parked_audits`), and so is a knowledge document's row (`postgres.parked_knowledge_deliveries`). An unavailable ClickHouse counts no attempt.

pg_durability.description: What an acknowledged write must survive: synchronous = a standby in another failure domain has flushed it (boot refuses a server with no synchronous standby); local = the primary's disk only (boot warns).

pg_erasure_evidence_hours.description: Hours an erased memory's id, or an erased knowledge document's `doc_id`, is kept as deletion evidence, refusing a write built from a head read before the erasure (longer than any request holds a head); a `namespace.restore` into its namespace leaves the memory out meanwhile.

pg_erasure_evidence_page_rows.description: Document ids an erasure reads from ClickHouse per statement, and keeps as deletion evidence per insert: what one page of a large scope holds in memory.

pg_lease_margin_seconds.description: Seconds before its lease ends that a publisher stops sending, for clock drift and the time a send takes to leave the process; under Postgres, shorter than both leases (`LOOM_PG_REQUEST_LEASE_SECONDS`, `LOOM_PG_DELIVERY_LEASE_SECONDS`).

pg_pool_max_size.description: Most connections the Postgres pool opens per process; a request waits for one.

pg_pool_min_size.description: Connections the Postgres pool keeps open per process.

pg_projection_wait_ms.description: Milliseconds an admission waits for earlier commits in its scope to reach search before answering 503 PROJECTION_BEHIND; a diagnostic report waits as long, then reads on and names `projection` in `skipped`.

pg_publish_interval_ms.description: Average ms between a process's publication flushes (one insert per table each), capped at half `LOOM_PG_PROJECTION_WAIT_MS`; bursts up to a second's worth; 0: none.

pg_request_lease_seconds.description: Seconds the writing request holds its revisions' delivery; past it, the delivery worker or a waiting admission in the namespace publishes them instead.

pg_restore_batch_rows.description: Memories one Postgres commit of a `namespace.restore` writes; each batch commits within a request's lease (`pg_request_lease_seconds`).

pg_statement_timeout_ms.description: Milliseconds a Postgres statement may run, and a request may wait for a pooled connection, before it fails.

platform_admins.description: Comma-separated login handles and emails promoted to platform_admin (org-wide visibility). A handle matches a password account's subject; an email matches only an IdP-verified (OIDC) email, never the unverified self-signup address. Empty = no platform admins.

policy_cache_ttl_seconds.description: Per-(org, namespace) rule cache TTL, seconds; other replicas see a rule change within it.

policy_max_window_seconds.description: Cap on any rule's look-back window, in seconds.

policy_mode.description: History policy over the agent trace: "off" reads/writes nothing; "shadow" records verdicts in loom.policy_decisions without blocking; "enforce" denies (403 POLICY_FORBIDDEN) and records them too. In enforce, writes fail closed on evaluation errors; reads never do.

procedure_strike_limit.description: `procedure.evolve` quarantines a procedure whose trace log ends in this many consecutive failed runs (out of procedure.match and the pack until a run succeeds). 0 = off.

profile_consolidation_cooldown_seconds.description: Seconds after a profile section is written before it is folded again.

profile_consolidation_enabled.description: Fold a user's durable preference/decision memories into a versioned profile section (memory_type='profile') for profile.render / context.pack; skipped when refreshed within the cooldown. LLM calls; namespace opt-in via consolidation_enabled.

profile_consolidation_max_identities_per.description: Users (org, namespace, user_id) one pass folds, most preference/decision rows first.

profile_consolidation_memory_limit.description: Memories read into one fold, highest confidence then newest first.

profile_consolidation_min_memories.description: Live preference/decision memories a user needs before a profile is folded.

profile_consolidation_model.description: Model of the profile fold, which consolidates an identity's memories into its profile; "" = `llm_model`.

projection_repair_enabled.description: Retry best-effort projections (chunks, evidence links, graph side tables) that failed after the primary write. Bounded and idempotent; unsupported ones stay in ops.projection_failures.list.

projection_repair_max_failures_per_pass.description: Recorded projection failures one pass retries (at least 1).

provider_check_timeout_s.description: Seconds a provider check (the dashboard's Models & keys validate and save) waits for its probe call before it reports `timeout`.

public_base_url.description: The address the server hands to clients — the client setups a new token comes with, `claude mcp add`, a bot's claim_url, OAuth metadata. Empty = the request's own Host and scheme, which only a loopback bind may rely on: a non-loopback bind_host refuses to start without it.

ratelimit_actor_fraction.description: Per-actor rate-limit bucket, keyed (namespace, token subject), as a fraction of the namespace limit. 1.0 = no actor bucket; 0.6 leaves a second credential budget while one sweeps.

ratelimit_class_fractions.description: JSON {class: fraction}: a traffic class carved into its own bucket of the base cap × fraction, so a bench sweep never spends production's budget. Class = token `traffic_class` claim, else namespace row, else request hint, else interactive. Absent class = 1.0 (base bucket).

ratelimit_shared.description: Share rate buckets across one server's web workers via a memory-mapped file, so a keep-alive client pinned to one worker sees the full cap. auto = when web_workers > 1; on = always; off = per-process buckets divided by replicas × workers.

ratelimit_shared_path.description: Bucket file; "" = one per server in the runtime dir (server/core/runtime_files.py). The file is 0600 and never opened through a symlink. Set it for two servers sharing one cap.

ratelimit_shared_slots.description: Table slots (32 bytes each). Every process of a server must agree; a mismatch falls back to per-process buckets and shows in /v1/health.

readiness_check_timeout_s.description: Seconds one readiness check may take; a slower check fails.

reads_llm_free.description: True: reads call no LLM (ask synthesis: 409), skip the spelling-fix and set-expansion embeddings, and rerank only as named, since a reranker is a model call.

ready_requires_mirrors.description: True: /v1/health/ready also waits until the mirror warm-up has queued its clones and while a clone of this host's git mirrors is running or queued (a failed clone does not hold it). Needs LOOM_CODE_MIRROR_WARMUP: without the warm-up nothing is cloned at boot and readiness does not wait for mirrors. Off by default: history ops answer `no_git_mirror` meanwhile.

recalibration_enabled.description: Periodically re-run the embedder calibration probe so thresholds follow a silently revised embedder. Fake providers skip.

reflection_distill_enabled.description: Reflection distillation: label recent sessions that carry no outcome (positive / negative / unclear into loom.session_outcomes_by_user), pair each confidently failed session with its nearest successful one and distil the difference into one hidden `reflection` memory. LLM calls; sessions labelled through run.complete are not re-judged.

reflection_distill_lookback_days.description: Days back a pass looks for unlabelled sessions and for failed sessions to contrast.

reflection_distill_max_contrasts_per_pas.description: Failed sessions one pass tries to pair and distil.

reflection_distill_max_judged_per_pass.description: Sessions one pass sends to the outcome labeller.

reflection_distill_min_confidence.description: A judged label below this confidence neither pairs nor is paired with.

reflection_distill_min_pair_similarity.description: Cosine floor between the failed and the successful summary; below it the sessions were not about the same thing.

reflection_distill_model.description: Reflection distillation: the outcome labeller and the contrast writer.

replica_count.description: The rate limiter divides every cap by the deployment's replica count so the replicas' sum matches the target (approximate, not cluster-strict). The count is the hosts with a live serving loom.instances row; this is its floor, and the count while those rows cannot be read.

require_real_providers.description: A fake or key-less provider is a `warn` in /v1/health `problems`; true (production) makes it an `error` and `status: degraded`, which preflight and monitors catch. Never changes the HTTP code (503 is ClickHouse-only).

restricted_audit_inline.description: Wait for the `namespace.restricted_access` audit row of each admitted restricted read before answering; false writes it beside the answer, lost if the process dies first.

restricted_serve.description: Kill switch for restricted namespaces. True: served to a principal whose token names the namespace AND who holds a live direct grant. False: every read is refused while ingest continues.

retention_audit_log_days.description: Days `loom.audit_log` rows are kept; 0 = forever. A person's Undo of a retirement holds by its record there: one aged out stops holding, and the conflict resolver may judge and retire that pair again.

retention_documents_days.description: Days `loom.documents` rows are kept; 0 = forever. The Postgres authority refuses it.

retention_memory_days.description: Days `loom.memory` rows are kept; 0 = forever. The Postgres authority refuses it.

retention_memory_embeddings_days.description: Days `loom.memory_embeddings` rows are kept; 0 = forever. The Postgres authority refuses it.

retention_reconcile_enabled.description: The supervisor re-applies table TTLs from settings + namespace rows on this timer as metadata changes (materialize_ttl_after_modify = 0): rows already past a new TTL leave at their part's next merge or a manual MATERIALIZE TTL.

retrieval_judge_model.description: The sampled retrieval judge (retrieval_judge_sample_rate). Deliberately a different model from the ones answering: a same-model judge measures agreement, not quality.

retrieval_judge_sample_rate.description: Fraction of searches sent to an independent LLM judge, written back as a `retrieval_relevance` score (unlike loom's own confidence scores, it shares no state with retrieval). 0.0 = off: it costs money per search; a few percent (e.g. 0.05) suits production.

runtime_dir.description: Directory of the files one server's web processes share (the rate-limit table); "" = chosen per process by server/core/runtime_files.py. scripts/serve.sh sets it once, before the workers start, so all of them name the same files.

runtime_overrides_refresh_seconds.description: Seconds between re-reads of loom.runtime_overrides (the admin rate-limit, latency-budget and live-setting overrides) in every process.

schema_status_ttl_s.description: Seconds the schema status (applied against shipped migrations) is cached for the health probe.

search_trace_log_enabled.description: Per-query recall telemetry into loom.search_trace_log (query, returned keys+scores, abstain, latency), fire-and-forget. Off by default: query text is logged, so it is an operator opt-in.

self_signup.description: Browser self-signup: "off" (endpoint 404s) or "open" (/v1/auth/self-signup mints JWTs scoped to the requested namespace). A non-loopback bind refuses "open" unless identity_provider is "trust-network", allow_insecure is set, or oauth_login_provider is "oidc" (which closes sign-up).

sensitivity_sweep_enabled.description: Daily sweep: re-label live rows written `sensitivity = ''` by a path that skipped the detector, as a new version per row; `high` rows' embeddings are tombstoned, never ALTER UPDATE. Covers the trailing window; the backlog is `loom sensitivity-sweep --apply`.

sensitivity_sweep_max_rows_per_pass.description: Rows one sensitivity sweep pass re-labels, and the keys per page it reads (at least 1).

sensitivity_sweep_pages_per_pass.description: Pages one sensitivity sweep pass reads at most, each of `sensitivity_sweep_max_rows_per_pass` keys (1 to 1000).

sensitivity_sweep_shapes.description: Shapes the sensitivity sweep applies (comma-separated: credential, email, phone, other); every high row is `credential`; `phone` and `other` (IBAN-only rows) are left to the operator's `loom sensitivity-sweep --apply`.

sensitivity_sweep_window_days.description: Days back the sensitivity sweep re-labels rows created in.

serves_traffic.description: False for a process no load balancer routes to (a workers-only container): its instance row does not count as a replica.

session_brief_llm.description: session.brief_save. `session_brief_llm` off = every brief comes from the deterministic builder (goal, status, files, errors, rules, pointers; no decisions or dead ends), except under an operator's extraction policy, where a save of events alone with no model to call writes nothing. The model is the deployment's LLM when `session_brief_llm_model` has no key. A save condenses its events into windows of `session_brief_window_chars` (≈6k tokens each) and revises the brief once per window, at most `session_brief_max_windows` calls per save (the last window takes the remainder, condensed harder).

session_brief_llm_model.description: Session briefs; without its provider's key the deployment's LLM writes them.

session_brief_max_windows.description: Most windows (and model revision calls) per brief save; the last window takes the rest.

session_brief_window_chars.description: Condensed size, characters, of one brief window (floor 2000); a window holds about three times this much raw event text before it is condensed.

shutdown_ready_delay_s.description: Seconds a process keeps serving after SIGTERM while /v1/health/ready answers 503, so the load balancer stops routing to it before its port closes. Size it to the LB's probe interval × failure threshold. 0 = stop at once.

storage_authority.description: Which store is the authority for live memory: clickhouse = ClickHouse alone; postgres = Postgres holds current content, revisions and delivery jobs, and ClickHouse serves search and history. Recorded at first boot; a replica configured for the other authority refuses to start.

storage_frontend_assets_retry_max_s.description: Longest wait, in seconds, between retries of a failed dashboard-asset publish (the wait doubles from storage_frontend_assets_retry_s).

storage_frontend_assets_retry_s.description: Seconds before a failed dashboard-asset publish round is retried, doubling up to `storage_frontend_assets_retry_max_s`.

structured_profile_backoff_base_seconds.description: Seconds a user or namespace whose structured profile build failed waits before the first retry; each further failure doubles it. Above 0.

structured_profile_backoff_cap_seconds.description: Longest wait, in seconds, of a user or namespace whose structured profile build keeps failing. Above 0.

structured_profile_cooldown_seconds.description: Seconds after a structured profile is built before new memories rebuild it; a schema change or a deleted source skips this wait. 0 rebuilds on the next pass.

structured_profile_enabled.description: Run the worker that builds each user's structured profile in the namespace's schema (LLM calls, only where `profile_schema.set` set one).

structured_profile_idle_interval_seconds.description: Seconds the structured profile worker waits after a pass that reached every namespace with a schema and took no user. Above 0.

structured_profile_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between structured profile passes. Above 0.

structured_profile_max_pass_seconds.description: Seconds a structured profile pass may run before the supervisor abandons it; it takes no user in the second half. Above 0.

structured_profile_max_users_per_pass.description: Structured profiles one pass builds; the namespaces in each page the pass reads share it equally, and the pass reads on while budget is left. At least 1.

structured_profile_memory_limit.description: Memories read into one structured profile build, highest confidence then newest first. At least 1.

structured_profile_model.description: Model of the structured profile builder, which fills a user's profile in the namespace's schema; "" = `llm_model`.

structured_profile_refusal_retry_seconds.description: Seconds a refused or cut-off structured profile build waits before it is tried again with nothing changed. Above 0.

structured_profile_scan_max_age_seconds.description: Seconds a namespace's scan for users behind their structured profile serves later passes before it is run again. Above 0.

structured_profile_scan_max_memory_bytes.description: Bytes of memory one namespace's structured profile scan may use (ClickHouse max_memory_usage). At least 1 MiB.

structured_profile_scan_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds one namespace's scan for users behind their structured profile may run; past it the scan fails and the namespace backs off. Above 0.

supervisor_lease_ttl_s.description: auto mode: seconds a lease holder that stops renewing keeps the workers before another process takes them over (failover time). At least 24: below that a renewal blocked for its 2 s timeout leaves no retry before the holder must give up (server/workers/leader.py has the timings).

task_lease_sweep_enabled.description: Lease sweeper: return expired leases to todo, resume deferred tasks at resume_at, escalate stale triage, and put right lease rows a race left out of step with their task.

task_lease_sweep_idle_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between task-lease sweep passes that found nothing.

task_lease_sweep_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between task-lease sweep passes while there is work.

task_webhook_batch_limit.description: Events one notice carries at most.

task_webhook_deliver_enabled.description: Post one Standard Webhooks-signed notice per new event batch to each inbox's webhook_url; the secret comes from the env var task_inboxes.webhook_secret_ref names (`LOOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET_<ORG>__<NAME>`, one of the inbox org's own).

task_webhook_deliver_idle_interval_secon.description: Seconds between webhook delivery passes that found no new event.

task_webhook_deliver_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between webhook delivery passes while notices are going out.

tenancy_mode_cache_s.description: Seconds (at least 1) a cell keeps its three rows (LOOM_CELL) and an org read as not held; LOOM_JWT_REVOCATION_MAX_STALE_SECONDS must be at least three times this.

tenant_max_concurrent_requests.description: Requests one org may have in flight at once, deployment-wide. Each process holds its share (divided by replicas × web workers, at least 1); a call over it gets 429 RATE_LIMITED. 0 = no cap.

tiering_agent_events_warm_days.description: Days before `loom.agent_events` rows move to the warm volume; 0 = never.

tiering_audit_log_warm_days.description: Days before `loom.audit_log` rows move to the warm volume; 0 = never.

tiering_chunks_warm_days.description: Days before `loom.chunks` rows move to the warm volume; 0 = never.

tiering_conversations_warm_days.description: Days before `loom.conversations` rows move to the warm volume; 0 = never.

tiering_documents_warm_days.description: Days before `loom.documents` rows move to the warm volume; 0 = never.

tiering_memory_embeddings_warm_days.description: Days before `loom.memory_embeddings` rows move to the warm volume; 0 = never.

tiering_memory_warm_days.description: Days before `loom.memory` rows move to the warm volume; 0 = never.

tiering_warm_volume_name.description: Volume named in tiering TTL clauses; must match a volume in the cluster's storage_policies.

tracker_bisect_component_dirs.description: The issue's component widens the scan to at most this many `src/` directories its PRs touch, each with `tracker_bisect_component_min_lift` × the share every trunk PR has (a hub directory says nothing); the aggregate is cached per component for `tracker_bisect_component_ttl_s`.

tracker_bisect_component_min_lift.description: A component directory counts only when its share of the component's PRs is at least this multiple of its share of every trunk PR.

tracker_bisect_component_ttl_s.description: Seconds the per-component directory aggregate is cached.

tracker_bisect_scope_patterns.description: When no frame resolves to a file, code.bisect_candidates(issue_number) scans the release window only for PRs whose diff carries one of this many of the issue's rarest patterns (IDF over the issue corpus). 0 turns the leg off.

tracker_checks_from.description: The FROM clause of the checks reads; '' = none. A tracker names its own (`checks` table, or its source entry's `checks.from`); this is the deployment-wide fallback. Name the table function, not a view over it: a view's filter runs on the QA side, so a hot test's read hits play's 1 GB result cap. ClickHouse's public CI (the `play` user is public) is "remoteSecure('play.clickhouse.com', 'default', 'checks', 'play', '')".

tracker_checks_repo.description: The repository whose CI `tracker_checks_from` is; '' = the namespace's only repository.

tracker_circuit_cooldown_s.description: Seconds an open breaker stays open before one probe read (at least 1 s).

tracker_circuit_failure_threshold.description: Consecutive failures of a tracker source's credential that open its breaker.

tracker_code_namespace_bindings_json.description: Which tracker namespace a code namespace reads its facts from: glob keys over the operator's repositories' namespaces → namespace, e.g. {"code-myrepo*": "tracker-myrepo"}; a code.repo.add_branch branch of one reads that repository's links. '' = no QA facts.

tracker_contract_check_budget_s.description: Seconds the tracker source contract check may take when a listing reports it.

tracker_contract_ttl_s.description: A source serves only while its schema meets the record contract (docs/features/tracker/record-contract.md), checked through its own credential once per this many seconds (at least 1 s); a failed check retries after 60 s.

tracker_dupcheck_duplicate_threshold.description: A draft's verdict: `duplicate_of` when the top candidate's calibrated confidence reaches this, `related` when any candidate reaches the related threshold, else `none` with no items. Both are probabilities from a logistic fit on labelled duplicate pairs, so they survive a refit; the scale is compressed. Measured `none` on 99% of negatives at 0.25.

tracker_dupcheck_duplicate_threshold_max.description: Upper bound of the fitted duplicate threshold.

tracker_dupcheck_duplicate_threshold_min.description: Bounds the fitted duplicate threshold is clamped into, so one odd fit cannot make every candidate (or none) a duplicate.

tracker_dupcheck_fanout_namespaces.description: How many tracker namespaces a duplicate check addressed to a code namespace (or its bound tracker namespace) reads when no `namespaces` list is given: every readable tracker record, the bound one first. 1 = the bound one only.

tracker_dupcheck_fit_negatives.description: Non-duplicate pairs sampled (by hash) per duplicate-check calibration fit.

tracker_dupcheck_fit_ttl_s.description: Seconds a namespace's stored duplicate-check fit is cached.

tracker_dupcheck_fix_path_days.description: The fix-in-flight leg reads PRs from the last this many days.

tracker_dupcheck_fix_path_prs.description: At most this many PRs the fix-in-flight leg reads per draft.

tracker_dupcheck_judge_body_chars.description: Body characters per candidate the judge reads.

tracker_dupcheck_judge_enabled.description: The judge stage. On a `related` answer one model call reads the draft against the top `tracker_dupcheck_judge_top_k` issue candidates' title + body head (`tracker_dupcheck_judge_body_chars`) and may promote a same-defect one to `duplicate` (never demotes; a recorded related_to never promotes). `tracker_dupcheck_judge_model` "" = default client. Benched on a labelled duplicate set.

tracker_dupcheck_judge_top_k.description: Issue candidates the judge reads (at least 1).

tracker_dupcheck_lead_min.description: A rerank `same` row at or above this is offered as a lead ("nearest reported: … — may be related, check it"), never as the verdict.

tracker_dupcheck_leg_retry_delay_ms.description: A leg whose read failed for a transient reason (a timeout, a connection error, an upstream 5xx) is run once more inside the op budget; one that still fails leaves the answer `epistemic: degraded` and `leg_status` names it with its reason. The pause before that retry, ms (at most 200).

tracker_dupcheck_leg_retry_min_ms.description: The shortest retry worth starting, ms: with less left the retry is skipped and `leg_status` says `retry_skipped_budget`.

tracker_dupcheck_leg_retry_reserve_ms.description: What the retry leaves of the op budget for the steps after the legs (hydrate, fit, judge), ms.

tracker_dupcheck_links_budget_s.description: Seconds the duplicate check's links and release reads may take together (measured p50 about 0.3 s).

tracker_dupcheck_pr_wait_s.description: Seconds the duplicate check waits for its related-PR search, which starts with the checks, once they finish.

tracker_dupcheck_recent_ttl_s.description: Seconds a duplicate-check answer is served again to the same caller for the same question.

tracker_dupcheck_refit_enabled.description: The fit (coefficients, curve, holdout) is JSON in loom.code_index_state under the tracker namespace, refitted by the tracker_links pass once older than `tracker_dupcheck_refit_interval_s` by replaying every gold query at its filing time. Off = the stored fit keeps serving; with none stored the op answers `uncalibrated`.

tracker_dupcheck_refit_interval_s.description: Seconds after which the tracker_links pass refits the duplicate-check calibration (7 days).

tracker_dupcheck_related_threshold.description: Calibrated confidence from which tracker.duplicate_check answers `related` (below `tracker_dupcheck_duplicate_threshold`).

tracker_dupcheck_rerank_body_chars.description: Body characters per candidate the rerank call reads.

tracker_dupcheck_rerank_enabled.description: The rerank stage. One model call reads the draft against a pool of each leg's own head (`tracker_dupcheck_rerank_per_leg` rows a leg) plus the issues the tracker graph links to the leading candidates; its same/related picks lead `nearest`, the verdict stays the fit's. Fails open.

tracker_dupcheck_rerank_ns_cap.description: At most this many candidates the rerank pool holds for one namespace's legs (after dedup, the legs taking turns).

tracker_dupcheck_rerank_per_leg.description: Rows each leg contributes to the rerank pool; also deepens the rows kept per leg when it exceeds the default head.

tracker_dupcheck_rerank_pool_cap.description: The candidates one rerank call reads (0 = dup_rerank.POOL_CAP, 40); 200 lets a 50-per-leg pool through a fan-out's namespaces.

tracker_dupcheck_rerank_timeout_s.description: Seconds the rerank call may take; past it the rerank reports error="timeout" and the verdict stands without it.

tracker_embed_batch.description: Items sent to the embedder in one call (at least 1).

tracker_embed_body_chars.description: Body characters embedded per item. Must stay under the embedder's 8,191-token input limit (a stack trace runs ~2 chars a token; one oversized text fails the whole batch). A change needs a re-embed (`loom tracker-embed-reset`, then the pass).

tracker_embed_closed_days.description: The embedding window for PRs, days: a PR closed longer ago is not embedded and one that leaves the window is tombstoned.

tracker_embed_enabled.description: Every interval (seconds), for each configured tracker namespace, the issues and PRs open or closed within `tracker_embed_closed_days` and changed since the last pass are embedded (`title + "\n" + left(body, tracker_embed_body_chars)`, `tracker_embed_batch` a call) into loom.qa_item_embeddings; an unchanged text (sha256) is skipped, an item that left the window is tombstoned. Off = nothing is written; the leg serves the table plus its query-time catch-up. The interval bounds only that catch-up, never what a query can find.

tracker_embed_fetch_multiplier.description: The nearest read's codes-shortlist over-fetch on loom.qa_item_embeddings (x10's misses are BFloat16 rounding only).

tracker_embed_issue_closed_days.description: The window for ISSUES, days (3650 = every closed issue the record holds): labelled duplicate targets are often closed long before the draft. PRs keep `tracker_embed_closed_days`.

tracker_embed_max_pass_seconds.description: Seconds a tracker-embed pass may run before the supervisor abandons it.

tracker_error_names_ttl_s.description: Seconds a namespace's error-name to code map is cached.

tracker_freshness_budget_s.description: Seconds the item-count read behind a tracker source's freshness may take.

tracker_links_enabled.description: A daily pass ranks, for every issue opened in the last `tracker_links_issue_days`, the merged trunk PRs of the `tracker_links_window_days` after it (from a week before) by BM25F over title and body, the issue's stack frames in the PR's diff, the closing mention and the component, and writes each issue's top `tracker_links_per_issue` into loom.qa_link_candidates. Off = nothing is written; `tracker.links` serves the table.

tracker_links_issue_days.description: Issues opened within this many days are ranked each pass.

tracker_links_max_pass_seconds.description: Seconds a tracker-links pass may run before the supervisor abandons it.

tracker_links_min_score.description: A consumer (code.backport_gap's issue path, the bisect's fix candidate) takes the top candidate as the fix only above this score AND when a closing keyword names the issue. tracker.links serves every row with its score.

tracker_links_per_issue.description: The top candidates written per issue into loom.qa_link_candidates.

tracker_links_weight_mention.description: Score = bm25_norm (the pair's BM25F as a share of the issue's best) + weight_mention × (1 closing keyword, 0.5 bare mention) + 0.05 × component_match. The stack-frames-in-diff features ride the row unscored.

tracker_links_window_days.description: Days after an issue opened in which a merged trunk PR is a fix candidate.

tracker_live_bisect_budget_ms.description: Budget of the bisect candidate read, which scans a release range's diffs, ms: a triage step, not an interactive one.

tracker_live_budget_ms.description: Caller-side budget per read, ms: past it the read is `tracker_unavailable` and counts against the breaker.

tracker_live_cache_ttl_s.description: Process cache TTL for live rows, seconds (upstream refreshes every 5–10 min); an empty result is kept at most 60 s.

tracker_live_checks_budget_ms.description: Budget of the per-test history read, ms: play scans the whole window by its time key, far past the 300 ms interactive budget.

tracker_live_serve.description: Kill switch: off = every tracker read answers `tracker_unavailable`.

tracker_live_text_budget_ms.description: Budget of the text-index reads (similar bugs, threads, changelog, PRs by path, area escalations / incidents by term), ms; above the 300 ms interactive budget.

tracker_live_timeout_s.description: Per-statement `max_execution_time` on the remote, seconds; the client's receive timeout is this plus 5 s.

tracker_org.description: The loom org the tracker namespaces belong to; empty (default) = none, so no tracker namespace serves and self-service sources are refused until it is set.

tracker_patch_line_timeout_s.description: Seconds one git call of the patch-history check may run.

tracker_restricted_repos_json.description: The repositories whose numbers name a restricted namespace's escalations and core incidents, as `Org/repo`: {"escalation": "Org/escalations", "incident": "Org/incidents"}. `escalation_context` / `incident_context` read the record `Org/repo#<number>`; a kind with no repository here reads no record by number.

tracker_self_service_allow_private_hosts.description: A registered host must resolve to a public address (no loopback, RFC 1918, link-local, CGNAT 100.64/10 or multicast); True lets a dev stack point at a local ClickHouse.

tracker_self_service_enabled.description: Self-service tracker sources: any signed-in org member registers one (`tracker.source.add`); credential and schema are checked before any write. Off = only the operator's map serves; loom.qa_sources rows are ignored.

tracker_self_service_max_sources.description: At most this many self-service sources an org may register; a further `tracker.source.add` is refused.

tracker_similar_agreement_max_rank.description: The deepest vector-leg rank that may boost a ranked candidate; 0 = any rank.

tracker_similar_agreement_weight.description: The agreement boost: a tracker.similar candidate found by a ranked leg AND the vector leg gains the vector leg's RRF contribution times this weight (1.0 = counts like a ranked leg, 0.5 = a tie-breaker) and the ranked set is re-sorted; vector-only candidates stay appended.

tracker_similar_catch_up_budget_ms.description: Ms the vector leg waits for its query-time catch-up (embedding the items changed since the tracker_embed pass's cursor), run beside the cosine scan. Past it the call answers from the table (`query.fresh_pending = true`) and the embedding finishes in the background for the next call.

tracker_similar_idf_ttl_s.description: Seconds the issue corpus's per-token document frequency (for BM25F) is cached per process; the upstream index cannot count it inside a budget.

tracker_similar_vector_leg.description: Whether tracker.similar's vector leg (over loom.qa_item_embeddings, filled by the `tracker_embed` pass) is in the default leg set; a caller naming `vector` in `legs` runs it regardless. The leg only adds candidates, after the ranked legs (`tracker_similar_agreement_weight` aside).

tracker_snapshot_ttl_s.description: Seconds a tracker source's status snapshot is reused.

tracker_source_check_timeout_s.description: Seconds tracker.source_check waits for a source's contract check.

tracker_source_connect_timeout_s.description: Seconds Loom waits to connect to a tracker source's ClickHouse. Read when a source's client is built, which is kept per credential.

tracker_sources_json.description: Every tracker source and the namespaces that read them: {"sources": {"<name>": {"host": "x.clickhouse.cloud", "port": 8443, "secure": true, "database": "loom_tracker"}}, "namespaces": {"qa-<team>": {"source": "<name>", "repos": ["Org/repo"], "restricted": false}}}. A namespace naming an unknown source does not serve (one error line, never a guess).

tracker_sources_refresh_seconds.description: How often a process re-reads loom.qa_sources (seconds); a write in this process refreshes at once.

tracker_test_candidates_timeout_s.description: Seconds the test-signal candidate read may take; it never holds up the answer.

tracker_test_daily_backfill_days.description: How far back a cold worker rolls, in days (the op's largest window is 90).

tracker_test_daily_budget_ms.description: Budget of one roll-up statement, ms.

tracker_test_daily_enabled.description: The tracker_test_daily worker rolls the CI table into loom.qa_test_daily once per day per test, so tracker.test_signal reads a key range here and the remote only for hours no roll-up covers. Off = the tables stop filling; the op falls back to the live read of the whole window.

tracker_test_daily_interval_seconds.description: Pass interval, seconds; today (and yesterday inside the settle lag) is re-rolled every pass as a partial day, so the live tail the op reads is at most one interval plus the current hour.

tracker_test_daily_lag_hours.description: Hours after a day ends before its roll is final: a check's row lands when the check finishes, not when it starts.

tracker_test_daily_max_days_per_pass.description: Days one test-daily pass rolls up: the shared `play` user is metered at 100 statements of one shape per hour, and the op's live reads share that quota.

tracker_test_daily_max_pass_seconds.description: Seconds a tracker test-daily pass may run before the supervisor abandons it.

tracker_test_daily_pace_s.description: Seconds paused between remote statements of a pass; 0 = no pause.

tracker_test_signal_churn_days.description: Churn window of the ledger leg, days (at least 1).

tracker_test_signal_cofail_k.description: Floor of K, the other failing tests an hour needs to be a storm hour.

tracker_test_signal_cofail_multiple.description: K, the other failing tests an hour needs to be a storm hour, is at least this multiple of the window's median failing tests per hour.

tracker_test_signal_cofail_prs.description: A storm hour spans at least this many PRs; a test failing on this many PRs in one hour is a shared cause by itself.

tracker_test_signal_cofail_share.description: Share of the test's failing hours that must be storm hours for `infra_candidate`.

tracker_test_signal_flip_rate.description: Status-change rate between consecutive runs of one PR/check sequence at or above which a test reads as flaky.

tracker_test_signal_min_runs.description: Runs of a test the history must hold before the test signal gives a verdict.

tracker_test_signal_smell_chunks.description: The static smell leg reads at most this many chunks of the test's home file(s) from the code plane (flaky-test smell tokens per category, counted).

tracker_test_signal_window_days.description: Window of the test-signal history read, days.

traffic_class_registry_ttl_seconds.description: How long a namespace's registry class is kept in the process cache.

trusted_callers.description: Comma-separated subjects allowed to send `X-Loom-On-Behalf-Of` (a trusted aggregator passing each end-user's identity under one service token). Empty disables the header.

trusted_proxies.description: Comma-separated peer addresses or CIDRs whose X-Forwarded-For/Proto headers uvicorn applies; any other peer's are ignored. "*" trusts all. Required behind a load balancer: at the default every client counts as the balancer's address for the sign-in and sign-up limits.

usage_fold_enabled.description: Fold loom.memory_usage_totals onto the ranking columns (reinforcement boost, memory.list sort_by=score, auto-promote gate); off, they freeze at write-time values.

vector_codes_state_probe_seconds.description: Seconds between re-reads of which vector columns are coded and which coded tables carry patch parts. A write that embeds reads again on its own when the reading is older than a few seconds (codes_state.FRESH_READING_S).

vector_search_quantized_codes.description: Send `vector_search_use_quantized_codes = 1` on vector-ranked reads whose column has a `Quantized(...)` codec and whose table has no patch parts: a codes-first scan plus full-precision rescore. A replica that rejects the setting (code 115) drops the fragment and retries.

vector_search_quantized_fetch_multiplier.description: Over-fetch for the codes-first read: stage 1 keeps LIMIT × this by code distance, stage 2 rescores. Only read when the codes setting is sent.

web_workers.description: uvicorn processes per container (the image's default: server.core.web_workers); the rate limiter counts N workers as N replicas.

worker_backoff_base_s.description: First wait, in seconds, after a worker's pass fails; it doubles per failure up to worker_backoff_cap_s.

worker_backoff_cap_s.description: Longest wait, in seconds, between a failing worker's passes (the wait doubles from worker_backoff_base_s).

worker_ledger_rows.description: One agent_events row per worker pass that spent something or failed (operation worker.<name>.pass, kind='worker'); loom.worker_status records every pass.

worker_partial_retry_s.description: A pass with a failed leg on a worker whose interval is longer than this retries after this long, doubling with each further such pass, up to the interval: a weekly pass must not leave one namespace's transient failure standing for a week.

workers_process.description: auto mode: where the lease holder runs the workers. child = a separate process it starts and stops with the lease, so the passes do not share the event loop that serves requests; inline = in the serving process.

workload_exchanges_per_agent.description: Workload-token exchanges one agent of a trust (a token with an agent claim) may make in 10 minutes, so one agent's loop cannot spend the trust's. A trust without agents has only `workload_exchanges_per_trust`.

workload_exchanges_per_trust.description: Workload-token exchanges (RFC 8693) one trust may make in 10 minutes, deployment-wide; past it /oauth/token answers 429 until older ones age out.
